    Latest Update: At the Races: Regional realignment

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1922 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Daniela Altimari, Mary Ellen McIntire and Niels Lesniewski.
    • New England is the ancestral home of moderate Republicans, from the Saltonstalls to the Bushes, whose fiscal conservatism and social moderation defined the national GOP for decades.
    • Last week, Yankee Republicans suffered a near-total wipeout.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniela Altimari, Mary Ellen McIntire and Niels Lesniewski.

    New England is the ancestral home of moderate Republicans, from the Saltonstalls to the Bushes, whose fiscal conservatism and social moderation defined the national GOP for decades.

    Last week, Yankee Republicans suffered a near-total wipeout. Maine’s Susan Collins, Latest England's last GOP senator, lost her seat to Democrat Troy Jackson, leaving former Maine Gov. Paul LePage, who just won a House seat, as the lone Republican headed to Congress from the region. (The picture was a bit brighter at the state level, where GOP Govs. Phil Scott of Vermont and Kelly Ayotte of New Hampshire were both reelected.).

    One Republican operative sees a path out of the wilderness in a post-Trump era. In an opinion piece in The Boston Globe, consultant Kristin Tate urged Latest England Republicans to focus on fiscal discipline and recognize that “independence from national party leadership can be a political asset, not an act of betrayal.”.

    After all, as the midterm election results remind us, no political realignment lasts forever.

    Three decades ago, there were plenty of moderate Democrats from Southern states serving in Congress, governor’s mansions and even the White House. But in the years since Bill Clinton's exit from the political stage, Democrats have largely written off the South.

    Recent findings suggest that which is partly why last week’s Democratic wins in the Carolinas, Georgia and, perhaps most notably, Mississippi were so stunning. All the elements that powered the party to victory nationally – disillusionment with Donald Trump, a rise in economic populism and hunger for change – played a role in the South as well.

    But other factors were unique to a region that has seen renewed attempts to dilute Black political power with the redrawing of House districts to favor the GOP.

    The Republican redistricting gambit in Southern states did not fully yield the desired results and seems to have helped galvanize Black voters and their allies, powering Democrats to unlikely victories.

    It’s too soon to say whether the GOP’s reduced hold on the South represents a temporary blip or an enduring shift.

    But Joe Trippi, a longtime Democratic strategist who advised candidates in Alabama and Florida this year, has a message for his party: “We need to invest in the South.”.

    #MSSEN: Democrat Scott Colom defeated GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction and the first in his party to win a Senate seat in the Magnolia State since 1982.

    Industry observers note that tar Heel tidal wave: Democrats in North Carolina have picked up at least five House seats, a striking development given the steep structural disadvantages the party faced. Prior to last week, no House Republican incumbent had lost a general election in the state since Republicans won control of the redistricting process more than a decade ago. And the Democratic gains could grow: In the 5th District, former journalist Chuck Hubbard narrowly leads 11-term Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx, and in the 3rd District, former state Rep. Raymond Smith holds a razor-thin edge over Republican Rep. Greg Murphy. The Associated Press had not called either race at publication time, though Murphy has conceded.

    Industry observers note that republicans pick campaign chairs: Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno and Georgia Rep. Brian Jack will be the chairs of Republicans’ respective campaign committees for the 2028 cycle. GOP lawmakers held their leadership elections Tuesday, as our colleagues Savannah Behrmann and John T. Bennett reported. Senate Republicans are sticking with South Dakota’s John Thune to lead them in the next Congress, while House Republicans picked former Freedom Caucus Chair Jim Jordan as their leader.

    Industry observers note that redistricting doubts: Maryland could be getting a new congressional map after voters approved a constitutional amendment that would clear the way for new lines in 2028. Our colleague Victor Feldman has more on the result and other election-related ballot measures across the country. But it’s not clear how many other states may look to redistrict next cycle after Republican efforts over the past 18 months largely didn’t pay off in last week’s elections.

    Recent findings suggest that run the table: With Rep. Darren Soto winning a sixth term in Florida, no Democratic incumbent lost reelection to a Republican this year. Soto’s win in a redrawn district also meant that Florida Democrats defended all four seats the GOP had targeted under a fresh congressional map.

    California contest: Rep. Ken Calvert defeated fellow Republican Rep. Young Kim in a rare member-versus-member contest for a redrawn Southern California seat that turned acrimonious. Republicans are poised to hold just four House seats in the Golden State after Democrats made good on five pickup opportunities under a latest congressional map.

    Cheesecake Factory caucus: The latest episode of the Political Theater podcast, hosted by Roll Call editor-in-chief Jason Dick, breaks down how candidates in both parties fared in counties where The Cheesecake Factory operates, after the popular chain restaurant became something of a side character in the closing weeks of the midterm campaign.

    Back to school: Newly elected members of Congress are on Capitol Hill this week for freshman orientation, an experience Massachusetts Rep.-elect Dan Koh told our colleague Nina Heller is “like high school – but it’s fun high school.” The incoming lawmakers took their class photo Thursday morning and will get to pick their Capitol Hill offices after next week’s famed lottery, Nina writes.

    It has been revealed that tracking the count: As of 4:30 p.m. Eastern time Thursday, House Democrats had flipped 44 seats, while Republicans had picked up three. Twelve races remain uncalled, including a pair in Louisiana that will be decided by December runoffs. On the Senate side, Democrats have flipped eight seats, with only Alaska’s race still undecided.

    Guv revision: Democrats flipped at least five governorships last week and will hold a majority of governor’s mansions next year. Two gubernatorial races remain uncalled by the AP: Kansas, where Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher is narrowly ahead of Republican state Senate President Ty Masterson, and Alaska, where Democratic former state Rep. Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins is just below the 50 percent threshold to win the election outright. In territorial elections, Republicans flipped the governor’s office in Guam while voters in the Northern Mariana Islands will pick their next governor in a Nov. 20 runoff.

    Sources indicate that #TNSEN: Republican Sen. Marsha Blackburn, who was elected Tennessee governor last week, is poised to pick her Senate successor. According to the Nashville Banner, the short list includes Knox County Mayor Glenn Jacobs, a former professional wrestler, Reps. Tim Burchett and Chuck Fleischmann, and Tennessee Deputy Gov. Stuart McWhorter.

    2028 on the brain: A handful of House Democrats are already considering 2028 Senate bids, according to Axios, including Kansas’ Sharice Davids, North Carolina’s Don Davis and Pennsylvania’s Chris DeLuzio.

    In a recent development, senator Morrison? Minnesota Rep. Kelly Morrison is earning buzz as a potential appointee to fill the Senate seat that Democrat Amy Klobuchar is vacating to become governor, Semafor reports. House Democrats aren’t likely to be as concerned about open seats as their Republican counterparts were in recent years, given the size of the incoming Democratic majority.

    AOC’s future: Progressive activists have rolled out a new organization to encourage New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for president in 2028. Meanwhile, Axios reports that Ocasio-Cortez has parted ways with the digital fundraising firm she’s worked with for several years and has brought on the same firm that Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders used during his two presidential campaigns.

    In a recent development, women lead: Shirley Emehelu is Upcoming Jersey’s new lieutenant governor after Democratic Gov. Mikie Sherrill picked her to succeed Dale Caldwell, who resigned in September amid sexual harassment allegations and other ethical lapses. New Jersey is now one of five states to have women in both the governor’s and lieutenant governor’s offices, along with Massachusetts, Arkansas, Iowa and Virginia. Iowa will come off the list next year after an all-male Democratic ticket swept this year’s gubernatorial race, though five other states elected women to both offices last week.

    According to recent reports, congress will once again be filled with losers – i.e, new members who have lost previous bids for elected office. Roll Call elections analyst Nathan L. Gonzales of Inside Elections returns to his biennial tradition as he runs down the latest list of “losers.”.

    In a recent development, ducking the wave: Democrats notched massive wins in unexpected places, but one state grew redder after last week’s elections. The New York Times checks in with voters in South Dakota, where the GOP won all nine statewide elections.

    Here come the MBAs: Democrats with corporate connections were among the winners in last week’s elections, countering the idea that candidates with serious business credentials have struggled within the party, The Wall Street Journal reports. The field of 19 winners with M.B.A. degrees includes Costco board member Helena Buonanno Foulkes, who won the Rhode Island governor’s race, and Paige Cognetti, a Goldman Sachs alum who flipped a House seat in Pennsylvania.

    How Ricketts did it: Nebraska Sen. Pete Ricketts’ election night success was one of the few bright spots for the GOP. Ricketts fended off a challenge from independent Dan Osborn by painting him as a Democrat, questioning his authenticity and highlighting leaked audio of his comments denigrating Trump voters, writes the Nebraska Examiner.

    Was it necessary? California redrew its congressional map to favor Democrats in response to Texas taking a similar step to boost the GOP. But some are questioning whether the state needed to cast aside its independent redistricting commission to rejigger the lines, given the scale of Democrats’ wins. “What they were literally saying is, ‘Let’s undo democracy to protect democracy,’” Lincoln Project co-founder Mike Madrid told CalMatters. “There’s something very Orwellian about it.”.

    Song of the cycle: The Upcoming York Times reviews “Talafreako,” an unlikely viral anthem celebrating the newly elected Democratic senator from Texas.

    History does rhyme: An opinion piece in The (Charleston) Post & Courier argues that the win by Democratic Sen.-elect Annie Andrews is the latest in a long line of cases in which South Carolina voters bucked the idea of party bosses picking their leaders.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Lufthansa has just revealed aims to introduce “real” business class seats on some of its narrow body planes, and that’s a really exciting development, given the typical business class standard on narrow body aircraft in Europe!
    • Interestingly, this is a concept that was initially trialed on Lufthansa Group low cost subsidiary Eurowings, and we knew at the time it was being used as a test for a more widespread implementation across the airline group.
    • Lufthansa has revealed that it will expand its premium offering on short and medium haul routes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Lufthansa has just revealed aims to introduce “real” business class seats on some of its narrow body planes, and that’s a really exciting development, given the typical business class standard on narrow body aircraft in Europe!

    Interestingly, this is a concept that was initially trialed on Lufthansa Group low cost subsidiary Eurowings, and we knew at the time it was being used as a test for a more widespread implementation across the airline group. I’m delighted to see this become more widespread, and I hope this is just the start of a bigger trend.

    Lufthansa has revealed that it will expand its premium offering on short and medium haul routes. With the introduction of the newly introduced Premium Business Seat, passengers will get more personal space than they’re used to on short haul aircraft.

    Industry observers note that historically, business class on Airbus A320-family aircraft has consisted of standard economy seats with a blocked middle. So that means with the 3-3 layout, four seats were only sold per row. What’s happening is that the first three rows on some aircraft are being replaced with two rows of recliner seats, meaning the per-seat footprint is around 50% bigger than in standard business class.

    At launch, the latest Lufthansa Premium Business Seat will be available on six Airbus A320 aircraft (and these planes will also be equipped with Starlink). The seat will feature significantly more space, with nearly one meter of legroom, plus extra recline. This doesn’t replace the standard business class product, but instead, is an upsell option.

    Sources indicate that this fresh product is now available for sale for flights as of March 1, 2027, on routes between Frankfurt (FRA) and Athens (ATH), Cairo (CAI), and Nice (NCE). However, the first plane with the seats will already be in service as of December 16, 2026, and as of February 2027, it’ll be deployed on the above routes (but tickets are only on sale as of March as of now).

    If a flight has this product available, you’ll see the “Premium Business Seat” designator during the booking process.

    The process of actually booking a Premium Business Seat is essentially an upgrade cost on top of the standard business class fare. For example, looking at a Frankfurt to Athens route, I see an upgrade cost of €139, which frankly seems quite reasonable for a flight of this length.

    Lufthansa is for the time being describing this as a commercial test, with the aim of examining demand for additional comfort on these routes, and the results will form the basis for deciding whether to expand the offering.

    You’ll see many people refer to short haul business class in Europe as a “scam” (I don’t agree, but people say that), and they’re shocked to find economy seats with blocked middles. Admittedly product standards differ vastly around the globe.

    The reason that airlines in Europe can get away with this product is threefold:.

    Keep in mind that most of the network carriers in Europe don’t make much money on short haul flights (or even lose a lot of money), given high costs and fierce competition from ultra low cost carriers.

    With that in mind, I think Lufthansa is going about this exactly right:.

    In a recent development, I’d love to see more airlines introduce something similar. In particular, Air France, as Europe’s most premium airline, seems best positioned to do this, and could do it with very little opportunity cost. Why?

    In a recent development, honestly, if I were Air France, I’d just introduce this throughout the A220 fleet, and it would be a major point of differentiation, competitively. No airline could do it as efficiently as Air France, and every A220 flight has at least two rows of business class, so the opportunity cost is minimal.

    Sources indicate that lufthansa will be introducing “real” business class seats on a subfleet of its Airbus A320s. As of the spring of 2027, expect these planes to be flying from Frankfurt to Athens, Cairo, and Nice. This Premium Business Seat concept will complement the existing business class, and will be available as a buy-up for business class passengers.

    Sources indicate that I’m very happy to finally see some more comfort on flights within Europe, and I imagine this will prove successful. If it doesn’t, I suspect it would be due to a lack of people knowing about this, rather than there not actually being demand.

    What do you make of the Lufthansa Premium Business Seat concept?

    Democrats mulling Iran war funding cutoff strategy

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A group of prominent Senate Democrats is pushing to use a must-pass spending bill to cut off funding for the Iran war, complicating the path toward a bipartisan deal for averting a partial government shutdown next month.
    • Tim Kaine, D-Va., stated Thursday he is working on legislative language ending the war that he wants attached to the next continuing resolution that is needed by Dec.
    • “I know it’s going to be my main push,” he remarked.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A group of prominent Senate Democrats is pushing to use a must-pass spending bill to cut off funding for the Iran war, complicating the path toward a bipartisan deal for averting a partial government shutdown next month.

    Recent findings suggest that sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., stated Thursday he is working on legislative language ending the war that he wants attached to the next continuing resolution that is needed by Dec. 11, when current funding runs out.

    “I know it’s going to be my main push,” he remarked. “I have to work with colleagues to try to find some language that works. And I’m not there yet, but I’ve told everybody that’s an opportunity.”.

    Democratic Sens. Michael Bennet of Colorado, Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, Tammy Duckworth of Illinois and independent Bernie Sanders of Vermont released a statement Thursday that they would oppose any deal that does not include “language that restricts the Trump Administration from using appropriated funds to continue his war against Iran.”.

    “When we vote on appropriations, we intend to fund the government and stop funds for this war,” the senators noted. “It is what the American people demand, and what they deserve.”.

    It is unlikely that Republicans, who are in control of both chambers of Congress until January, not to mention the Oval Office beyond that, would agree to such a deal.

    House Appropriations Chairman Tom Cole, R-Okla., said earlier this week that “a Republican Congress is not going to send bills to a Republican president that he's going to veto.”.

    While ending the war is a top priority of Democrats as they take back power in the newly introduced Congress, insisting on doing so this year could lead to a Christmas-time partial government shutdown. If a shutdown starts after Dec. 11, it’s possible it would still be ongoing when Democrats take control of both chambers in January.

    But some Democrats appeared to still be weighing how rapidly to push for a cutoff of war funding.

    Senate Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash, said that whether or not Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth remains in his job, “we’re still going to have language stopping this war.”.

    She was coy on whether that fight would take place on the anticipated continuing resolution in December or wait until next year when Democrats take back power, saying that lawmakers are “looking at all options.”.

    Sources indicate that democrats are committed to ending the "reckless and costly war of choice in Iran," House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., noted Thursday. He deferred to House Appropriations ranking member Rosa DeLauro, D-Conn., "to see what’s possible in advance of Dec. 11" in talks with the other top appropriators.

    "I don’t want to get out ahead of Congresswoman DeLauro, but House Democrats have uniformly opposed providing any additional money to Donald Trump’s war machine. to Pete Hegseth’s war machine, over in the Middle East," Jeffries said.

    It’s not clear how long a potential continuing resolution would last, and DeLauro mentioned earlier this week that she wants it to be as short as possible.

    The Office of Management and Budget has not yet submitted “anomalies” — changes to the current spending levels to be included in the continuing resolution — to Congress.

    It has been revealed that the administration is considering options including a stopgap bill that would run through March, sources familiar with the talks stated. But no decision on the timing covered by the anomalies has been made.

    Aris Folley, Jacob Fulton and Michael Macagnone contributed to this report.

    • Industry observers note that american Express owns both Resy and Tock (which is now being integrated into Resy), as part of its larger “lifestyle” play for attracting card members.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Resy has just rolled out the Resy Rewards program, which lets American Express card members in the United States earn an extra 4x points per dollar spent at participating Resy restaurants, on top of their credit card rewards. As you’d expect, it’s not quite that straightforward, but I’d still consider this to be pretty exciting!

    Industry observers note that american Express owns both Resy and Tock (which is now being integrated into Resy), as part of its larger “lifestyle” play for attracting card members. So along with that, Resy is leaning more into the rewards program side of things, with the new Resy Rewards program offering an extra 4x Amex points per dollar spent at eligible Resy restaurants.

    Resy Rewards is first launching in New York City, where users will see a new “Rewards” tab within the Resy iOS app, where they can browse and book eligible restaurants. Restaurants participating in the Resy Rewards launch include Carne Mare, Le Crocodile, Hearth, Kiko, OPTO, Le Pavillon, and more. In 2027, Resy Rewards plans to expand to additional U.S. cities, and select Tock venues will become eligible to participate in the program.

    According to recent reports, so, how exactly does Resy Rewards work? Card members need to enroll a US-based Membership Rewards program eligible card in Resy Rewards, then book a Resy Rewards reservation through the “Rewards” tab in the Resy iOS app, and then pay the bill for the dining experience with the enrolled card. So this requires a little more jumping through hoops than just using an Amex card Resy credit, for example.

    Recent findings suggest that these rewards are in addition to whatever the standard rewards are on an Amex card. For example, the American Express® Gold Card (learn more) ordinarily earns 4x points at restaurants globally, so if you dined at a restaurant eligible for Resy Rewards, you could be earning 8x points per dollar spent, which is pretty awesome.

    Here’s how Pablo Rivero, CEO of Resy and SVP of American Express Global Dining, describes this:.

    “For the first time, we’re bringing American Express’s industry-leading Rewards program into the Resy iOS app and connecting two things our Card Members value deeply: great dining experiences and meaningful rewards. As we’ve seen with the success of the Resy Credit, rewarding diners while driving demand and revenue to Resy restaurants is a win on both sides of the table.”.

    I’m delighted to see Amex introduce an opportunity to earn points for dining out, beyond the bonus categories already offered on some of the issuer’s most popular cards. For the time being, this is rather niche, given that it’s limited to select restaurants in Latest York City, but the expectation is that it will expand more broadly in 2027 (though it remains to be seen how broadly).

    Essentially think of this as being similar to a dining rewards program, as the idea is that restaurants have to opt-in to participate in this, with the hope being that this drums up business for them (and presumably they pay Amex and Resy something extra in exchange for that).

    Furthermore, you do have to specifically reserve your reservation through Resy to qualify for this, so if you don’t have a reservation made through the “Rewards” tab on Resy, then you won’t earn bonus points.

    I’m happy to see this, as earning 8x points on dining when paying with the Amex Gold Card is quite a great deal. Then again, so much of my dining out is through InKind, which is my favorite dining rewards program, given the excellent selection of restaurants the program has in Miami, and it’s tough to compete with the rewards offered by the program.

    Recent findings suggest that the new Resy Rewards program offers bonus Amex points when you make a reservation at an eligible restaurant and then pay with your eligible Amex card. The idea is that you can earn an extra 4x points per dollar spent on purchases at eligible restaurants, which is pretty awesome.

    The catch is that this is initially launching in New York City, only “eligible” restaurants qualify, and you need to reserve through Resy and then pay with the same linked card in order to earn the bonus points. It’s nice to see this launch, and I look forward to it expanding to more markets.

    In a recent development, american Airlines is replacing the cards it hands passengers when their flights fall apart. The newly introduced Travel Assistance Card points customers to rebooking, baggage tracking, eligible vouchers and other help. And employees are being told to do more than hand over the card and send passengers away. An internal memo set this week as the start date at domestic airports. Use the Travel Assistance Card as a guided customer support tool, not simply as a handout. That’s a small change in what American hands customers, with a much bigger expectation for what employees are supposed to do. What Replaces The RICAP Card I’ve written about American’s RICAP cards and the special phone number printed on them. The name stands for Reservations Irregular Ops Customer Assistance Program. Airport agents gave them to customers affected by delays and cancellations, providing a way to get rebooked when airport lines were long. American periodically changed the number. The new version provides web addresses and QR codes for: Rebooking and baggage tracking. Eligible vouchers and refund information. Answers to common questions, chat support, the American Airlines app and additional travel assistance. Robert Isom included disruption recovery technology in his plan to reclaim American’s premium reputation. At a gate with one employee, though, boarding the next departure and walking several stranded customers through their options compete for the same person’s time. This memo gives that employee another task. It doesn’t add anyone else to help.     General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    Delta SkyMiles & World Of Hyatt Partnership Live: Dual Earning, Milestone Rewards, & Linking Accounts

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1305 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In September 2026, Delta SkyMiles and World of Hyatt unveiled plans to launch a fresh, long term strategic partnership.
    • Recent findings suggest that at the time, we didn’t actually have any details as to what the partnership would entail, but that has now changed, as additional information has been revealed.
    • Delta and Hyatt are launching a fresh loyalty program collaboration, which comes with a “shared ambition to create additional value, recognition and engagement opportunities across more of the travel journey.” This includes reciprocal opportunities to earn rewards, and also reciprocal opportunities to select perks with the partner brand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In September 2026, Delta SkyMiles and World of Hyatt unveiled plans to launch a fresh, long term strategic partnership. This announcement came just shortly after American AAdvantage and World of Hyatt revealed that they will be ending their partnership.

    Recent findings suggest that at the time, we didn’t actually have any details as to what the partnership would entail, but that has now changed, as additional information has been revealed. Parts of the partnership are even now live, and members can already link their accounts.

    Delta and Hyatt are launching a fresh loyalty program collaboration, which comes with a “shared ambition to create additional value, recognition and engagement opportunities across more of the travel journey.” This includes reciprocal opportunities to earn rewards, and also reciprocal opportunities to select perks with the partner brand.

    Here’s how Laurie Blair, Hyatt’s SVP of Global Marketing and Loyalty, describes this:.

    Sources indicate that “World of Hyatt and Delta SkyMiles were each built to make travel more meaningful and rewarding, which makes this collaboration feel meant to be. By connecting the Delta flight and Hyatt stay, we are helping members get more from the journeys they are already taking while opening the door to new experiences, destinations and memories. It is an exciting next step in our commitment to caring for members throughout the full travel journey, from takeoff to check out.”.

    Here’s how Dwight James, Delta’s SVP of Customer Engagement & Loyalty, describes this:.

    In a recent development, “At Delta, we know loyalty is something we earn by delivering meaningful value and experiences that make our Members want to keep choosing us. Our relationship with World of Hyatt gives us another way to do that by recognizing and rewarding Members across more of their travel, while creating fresh ways to earn, engage and experience both brands.”.

    It has been revealed that effective immediately (as of November 17, 2026), elite members of both loyalty programs can earn simultaneously with the fresh “Dual Earn” benefit. Members must link their accounts, and can then earn additional rewards.

    World of Hyatt members can earn bonus points on eligible Delta flights (which includes Delta Comfort, Delta Premium Select, Delta First Class, and Delta One), as follows:.

    Delta SkyMiles members can earn bonus miles on eligible Hyatt stays (which includes qualifying room rates, qualifying incidental spend, and qualifying non-stay charges at participating Hyatt properties, eligible Mr & Mrs Smith spend booked through Hyatt, and eligible spend at The Venetian booked through Hyatt):.

    According to recent reports, as of 2027, eligible elite members of both World of Hyatt and Delta SkyMiles will gain access to new milestone reward choices, giving people more ways to earn, and more flexibility in how they use their loyalty benefits. This would apply to World of Hyatt Milestone Rewards, and Delta SkyMiles Choice Benefits.

    Industry observers note that as of January 1, 2027, World of Hyatt members will be able to choose Delta awards as they reach qualifying Milestone Rewards thresholds. The first Delta award choice will become available at 20 qualifying nights or 35,000 base points, with additional choices as members progress through the program, including:.

    As of February 1, 2027, Delta SkyMiles members will be able to choose Hyatt awards as they reach qualifying Choice Benefits thresholds. Members will be able to select free night awards, as follows:.

    To celebrate the start of this partnership, Hyatt and Delta are offering limited time offers for members who link their accounts.

    First, from November 17 through December 31, 2026, linked members can register to earn one additional World of Hyatt elite night after completing their first qualifying Hyatt stay during the offer period. Taking advantage of this should be a no-brainer.

    Next, from January 4 through February 15, 2027, linked members can:.

    Sources indicate that basically, Hyatt has dumped American in favor of Delta. Admittedly the partnership between American and Hyatt had already been scaled back over time. The two programs used to offer a dual accrual opportunity as well, but that was eventually cut.

    After all, companies only want to offer perks like that if they’re driving incremental business, and I imagine at some point it’s hard to justify that expense, when you feel like there’s not much upside left:.

    Sources indicate that now the Delta and Hyatt partnership is starting out in a similar way to how the American one did, with one major exception. On the dual accrual front, SkyMiles elite members are lucky, as they earn rewards on all qualifying Hyatt spending. Meanwhile World of Hyatt members only earn rewards when booking premium tickets, which is a bit disappointing. And here I was thinking that all seats on Delta aircraft are premium!!

    I do have to say, as much as I’m a World of Hyatt loyalist, the program has certainly become less differentiated over time. While Delta can argue all it wants about how premium it is, SkyMiles simply isn’t as good of a loyalty program as AAdvantage. So perhaps this swap reflects the direction Hyatt is trying to head on loyalty… I dunno.

    Recent findings suggest that delta and Hyatt have rolled out an exclusive new partnership, which explains why American and Hyatt cut ties. The partnership is now live, and it includes dual points accrual opportunities, reciprocal milestone perks, and some limited time opportunities.

    At a minimum, it’s definitely worth linking accounts. And if you’re a World of Hyatt member with a stay planned before the end of the year, be sure to register for an extra elite night, as there’s no reason not to take advantage of that.

    What do you make of this new Delta and Hyatt partnership, and American being dumped?

    In a recent development, membership is free and takes no more information than commenting as a guest. Earn status points for good contributions, and see fewer ads as your status grows.

    Your feedback is important in helping us keep our community safe.

    The comments on this page have not been provided, reviewed, approved or otherwise endorsed by any advertiser, and it is not an advertiser's responsibility to ensure posts and/or questions are answered.

    This is all pretty similar to what JAL did with Marriott-Bonvoy this year, and what ANA is doing with IHG from next year.

    Agree with grayanderson, a couple thousand extra points a year is a nice bonus, not a reason to switch. IMO the cash rate on the Hyatt itself moves the needle far more than dual earn. FWIW free tools like Arbitrica or similar look up the same hotel from somewhat 200 countries to find kind of the lowest price in the world, since prices and inventory differ by country. Then link the accounts anyway, it takes two minutes.

    It seems odd to only give points to elites. I'd think giving a couple of thousand points to someone not right now engaged in the program might be a good way to entice them in.

    Industry observers note that I feel like those choice awards are deluded on the Delta end. The credits with Delta might actually be vaguely useful for the lower tier milestones (20/30), however? The rest of this is...nice, I guess, but not likely to make much difference in my travel patterns? It's probably an extra 2-3k WoH points and an extra 5k SkyPesos per year for me, and ignore most of the noise?

    Snoozefest. Will get killed in a year when Hyatt realizes how costly/non-incremental it is and what a terrible partner Delta is. Also the milestones don't even make sense. At 60 nights, there is no selectable milestone, which is what these are described as. Unless Hyatt about to announce some changes.

    Latest Update: Belgrade is having a moment: Why you should visit Serbia's capital in 2027

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1570 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that you might have seen Serbia in the news lately.
    • The jubilant energy unleashed, combined with the Serbian capital’s soon-to-shine spotlight as it prepares to host the 2027 World Expo make now the perfect time to initiative your visit to Belgrade.
    • Sleepier than some other European capitals, yet vibrant and buzzing with a construction boom, Belgrade is coming into its own.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that you might have seen Serbia in the news lately. The country’s recent national elections enacted a political sea change spearheaded by student groups seeking greater freedoms and opportunities.

    The jubilant energy unleashed, combined with the Serbian capital’s soon-to-shine spotlight as it prepares to host the 2027 World Expo make now the perfect time to initiative your visit to Belgrade. That’s why the city made our list of top destinations for next year.

    Sleepier than some other European capitals, yet vibrant and buzzing with a construction boom, Belgrade is coming into its own. It’s also easier than ever to get there, thanks to plentiful airline connections not only to other European hubs but also to the U.S. via the country’s national carrier, Air Serbia.

    So start your points planning and make Belgrade a part of your next transatlantic trip.

    The fastest way to get to Belgrade’s Nikola Tesla Airport (BEG) from the U.S. is aboard Air Serbia from Chicago’s O’Hare International Airport (ORD) or Latest York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK). The airline also recently confirmed that it will launch twice-weekly service to Miami International Airport (MIA) in May 2027.

    Air Serbia’s main major airline partner is Etihad, so your best bet for booking award tickets is to use Etihad Guest miles. The program is a transfer partner of:.

    Sources indicate that that noted, award availability is hard to come by since these flights only operate a few times a week. Instead, you might want to consider redeeming Flying Blue miles for flights on Air France via Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport (CDG) or via Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (AMS) on KLM.

    For Star Alliance flyers, award availability between the U.S. and Belgrade is plentiful on carriers like LOT via Warsaw Chopin Airport (WAW) and Lufthansa via Frankfurt Airport (FRA) or Munich International Airport (MUC) and Swiss via Zurich Airport (ZRH), starting at 42,500 Aeroplan points each way in economy and 75,000 Aeroplan points each way in business class. Taxes and fees range from about $100 to $150 in each direction.

    Aeroplan is a transfer partner of:.

    Industry observers note that belgrade is expecting to see its first Intercontinental open in early 2027, just in time for the World Expo. Until then, there are plenty of other hotels where your points will come in handy.

    In a recent development, located in the new riverside Belgrade Waterfront District, which is home to a sprawling luxury mall, a promenade with tons of bars, cafes and restaurants, and more than a few high-rise apartment buildings, the St. Regis Belgrade opened in November 2024 in a striking glass-and-steel tower. The hotel has just 119 spacious rooms and suites with floor-to-ceiling windows, a beautiful spa with an indoor pool, a cafe-patisserie, a continental restaurant and an outpost of the brand’s signature St. Regis Bar. Rates start at $290 or 43,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night.

    It has been revealed that the Hyatt Regency Belgrade is a comfortable, modern hotel in Novi Beograd, the city’s main business district, across the Sava River from the historic core, so it’s not the best for leisure travelers. That mentioned, you can’t beat nightly rates that start at $148 or 6,000 World of Hyatt points per night.

    In a recent development, the Hilton Belgrade is centrally located near Slavija Square, within walking distance of attractions like the Nikola Tesla Museum and the Church of Saint Sava. It has 242 rooms and suites and a restaurant that serves contemporary Serbian cuisine. Rates start at $170 or 50,000 Hilton Honors points per night.

    Industry observers note that you won’t find Uber in Serbia, but taxis are plentiful and can be hailed via apps like Yandex, Pink Taxi Nova and Car:Go. The apps make it easy to pay with a credit card. Just be sure to use a credit card that earns bonus points on ride-hailing services or on travel charges in general.

    Sometimes drivers will not accept rides unless you are paying cash, though, which you can also book through the app and then take a metered ride. So be sure to pull some cash out at the ATM at the airport before heading into the city.

    Once in Belgrade, it’s easy to get around by public trams and buses, which are free to use within the city center.

    Related: The best credit cards for commuting expenses.

    Industry observers note that for a city of its size, Belgrade’s restaurant scene is surprisingly diverse. Of course, you should make it a priority to try typical Serbian dishes like grilled cevapi sausages with fluffy bread and ajvar red pepper sauce, and sarma, which is pickled cabbage stuffed with spiced meat and rice, not to mention the plethora of cured meats and mountain cheeses. Bela Reka is a great place to try a smattering of Serbian specialties, many of them sourced from the restaurant’s own farm in the Homolje Mountains.

    Perched on the riverbank, Suvenir serves traditional dishes like roasted lamb and bacon-wrapped prunes in a beautiful setting.

    In a recent development, for a contemporary take on Balkan cuisine, Iva is a sophisticated hideaway tucked into a courtyard near Saint Sava church where age-old dishes are reinterpreted through a modern lens. The piping-hot burek pastries stuffed with cheese, baked peach, hot pepper and honey are not to miss ($12), as is the confit river pike-perch with gnocchi and charred Swiss chard in a white wine sauce ($20). A glass of crisp Deuric Severna Morava white wine from the Fruska Gora region is the perfect accompaniment ($7).

    Be sure to book ahead for a table at S5 by Angie, a fine-dining bolthole hidden in an otherwise unremarkable apartment building in the city’s quiet Zemun district. Spend a while enjoying a cocktail in the living-room-like parlor, complete with a vinyl record collection, then settle in for a multicourse feast prepared by chef "Angie" Risimic that might include dishes like creamy labneh with tart tomatoes, fluffy ravioli with mild ricotta-style cheese doused in a green herb and blackberry sauce with trout roe, and tender pork in a rosehip demi-glace with end-of-summer morels. Prix-fixe menu prices vary but range from $75-$150, though a la carte ordering is also possible.

    For something more casual, spend an evening strolling cobblestones of Skadarska Street in the bohemian neighborhood of Skadarlija, just a short walk from Republic Square, where you will find over a dozen traditional kafane, or taverns, serving similar menus of hearty dishes along with plenty of plum-flavored rakija spirits.

    Tri Sesira, or the Three Hats, was a favorite of the Serbian Romantic poet and painter Dura Jaksic, a statue of whom sits outside his humble former house nearby.

    Belgrade has a handful of worthwhile museums, but not so many as to commandeer your entire timeline.

    According to recent reports, the National Museum has exhibits ranging from prehistoric artifacts to medieval Balkan icons, Italian Renaissance and Flemish masters, French Impressionists and modern artists, including pieces by well-known Yugoslav painters like Sava Sumanovic. Entrance is $3 for adults.

    It’s free to stroll the grounds of Belgrade Fortress and Kalemegdan Park, which overlook the confluence of the Danube and Sava Rivers and are popular places for sunset meetups.

    According to recent reports, some of the museums at the fortress have their own entrance fees and operating hours. The citadel dates to the third century B.C.E., though it has seen hundreds of battles and been destroyed, rebuilt and expanded dozens of times in the ensuing millennia.

    Even if churches aren’t your thing, no visit to Belgrade would be complete without a stop at the brilliant white, copper-domed Church of Saint Sava, which is one of the largest Eastern Orthodox churches in the world.

    The interior mosaics gleam with gold and are utterly breathtaking. Entrance is free.

    In a recent development, nearby the Nikola Tesla Museum is a fun, interactive affair. It offers guided tours every 45 minutes, but they fill up fast, so get there at least half an hour before the next one to line up. Entrance costs $7.50 and includes a short film, then demonstrations using Tesla coils before a small exhibit spanning the inventor’s life and some of his personal effects.

    Sitting in a small park of its own, the Museum of Yugoslavia is a memorial to the former country’s late strongman, Josip Broz Tito, who rose to prominence in the resistance to the Nazi occupation of World War II and eventually oversaw every aspect of life in Yugoslavia until his death in 1980.

    In a recent development, the complex includes his mausoleum — the so-called “House of Flowers” — an older building with some of his personal belongings and displays about daily life in Yugoslavia and a larger wing with temporary exhibits including a recent one on themes of propaganda in wartime. Admission is $7.50 for adults.

    The pedestrian shopping street of Knez Mihailova is also well worth a wander, if only for unique souvenirs produced by Serbian craftspeople at the Belgrade Window boutique.

    According to recent reports, it might not have been on your radar before, but Belgrade is well worth a visit, especially with all the events on the calendar for 2027, including hosting the World Expo. Along with some luxurious new hotels and a growing crop of exciting new restaurants, plus a small but impressive cadre of museums and galleries, it might just become one of your favorite European capitals.

    British Airways Launches Major Newly introduced 24-Hour Route In 7 Weeks: See Map Now

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (795 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that british Airways will finally reintroduce service to Melbourne in early January.
    • The carrier last flew there more than 20 years ago, in March 2006.
    • Industry observers note that OAG data shows that the oneworld member will take off from London Heathrow to Melbourne on January 9, 2027.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that british Airways will finally reintroduce service to Melbourne in early January. Melbourne is the capital of the Australian state of Victoria and is now the nation's second most populous city based on the significant urban area population. It is also Australia's fastest-growing state capital by people added.

    The carrier last flew there more than 20 years ago, in March 2006. That was when the UK's largest long-haul operator deployed the now long-retired Boeing 747-400. Things will be very different this time.

    Industry observers note that OAG data shows that the oneworld member will take off from London Heathrow to Melbourne on January 9, 2027. 20 years ago, flights operated via Singapore, but they'll now do so via Kuala Lumpur. This may also help to shore up the performance of Heathrow-Kuala Lumpur flights. Covering 9,134 nautical miles (16,916 km) each way on a great circle, but not real-world, basis, the new route to Melbourne will be the airline's new second-longest offering.

    Recent findings suggest that BA will deploy the Boeing 787-9 to Victoria, with both the 215-seat and 216-seat configurations used. This might not seem like a big difference, but it perhaps is, especially on such a long trip. The 216-seater has the airline's older business seats, while the 215-seat alternative has the newer cabin.

    Kuala Lumpur to Melbourne (fifth freedom rights).

    Melbourne to Kuala Lumpur (fifth freedom rights).

    The configuration with the better product is due to operate 57% of the time between January and October next year. This includes the inaugural service. The 215-seat so-called Dreamliner, to use the Boeing moniker, has eight seats in first class, 38 in business, 39 in premium economy, and 130 in economy. Despite not having the newest cabins, this layout is slightly less premium. 21% of capacity is in first/business, against 23% on the 216-seater.

    According to recent reports, in the 12 months to August 2026, booking data indicates that 1.4 million round-trip passengers flew between Europe and Melbourne. Excluding seasonality, around 3,800 people did so daily. Nearly half of the market flew with Emirates, Etihad Airways, and Qatar Airways via the Gulf or with Singapore Airlines via Changi. The quartet collectively benefits from lots of flights to Melbourne, while the Middle Eastern operators, in particular, have big European networks. Their dominance may reduce slightly, at least in specific markets, as four carriers will now fly between Melbourne and Europe, with three being European.

    Their dominance may reduce slightly, at least in specific markets, as four carriers will now fly between Melbourne and Europe, with three being European. They include Finnair, whose debut in Australia, as unusual as that might appear, was in late October 2026. The oneworld member runs daily (which is even more surprising) on the Airbus A350-900 via Bangkok, with fifth freedom rights.

    In the northern winter, Finnair has three daily flights from Helsinki to the Thai capital. As such, extending one flight to Australia during the cold season in the north with greater aircraft availability is less dramatic than might otherwise be the case. Significantly, it is the only EU airline to fly to Australia.

    Heathrow to Melbourne via Kuala Lumpur.

    Finnair to Melbourne via Bangkok.

    Istanbul to Melbourne via Singapore.

    Recent findings suggest that turkish Airlines, whose Istanbul Airport hub is on the European side of the Bosphorus, also operates. Despite having lots of unused traffic rights to Australia, the carrier's frequency remains unchanged compared to when the long route began. This could be a sign of insufficient performance or a lack of widebodies. BA's return rounds out the European side of the equation. All three operators fly via a different city in Southeast Asia to benefit from the local traffic.

    Recent findings suggest that qantas has a long history of flying from Melbourne to Europe. For example, the oneworld member — there's a trend here — flew to Heathrow via Singapore (QF9/QF10) or Hong Kong (QF29/QF30) for years on the 747-400 and later via Singapore on the A380. The Kangaroo Route then switched to flying via Dubai on the A380 in partnership with Emirates (QF9/QF10).

    In 2018, when the 787-9 appeared, the routing changed again, flying via Perth on a same-plane basis (QF9/QF10). Late last month, Qantas reintroduced a one-stop, same-plane, same-flight-number operation from the UK's busiest airport to Melbourne via the capital of Western Australia.

    Due to the ongoing war in Iran, the 787-9 does not currently begin in Melbourne on a same-flight-number basis. Avoiding Iranian airspace means that the aircraft does not fly nonstop from Perth to Heathrow, stopping in Singapore instead. The total operation is Perth-Singapore-Heathrow (as QF219, not QF9), and then Heathrow-Perth-Melbourne (QF10). While subject to change, starting and ending in Melbourne is due to return on March 28, 2027.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that barry Goldwater was acquainted with political setbacks.
    • It has been revealed that after the loss, Goldwater urged his supporters not to give up the fight for free markets, smaller government, and the American family.
    • Victor Riches is the President and CEO of the Goldwater Institute, leading the Institute’s efforts to help people in all 50 states live freer, happier lives.

    It has been revealed that barry Goldwater was acquainted with political setbacks. The morning after the 1964 presidential election, he could count the states he had won on two hands. Harder to number were the Americans who had spent that fall knocking on doors for the first time because a senator from Arizona had given voice to something they believed. Goldwater had asked them to help Americans reclaim power from Washington.

    It has been revealed that after the loss, Goldwater urged his supporters not to give up the fight for free markets, smaller government, and the American family. It was the collective conviction that Americans could build better lives for their families if they could keep more of what they earned and decide for themselves how to raise their children that kept these people invested in American politics.

    Victor Riches is the President and CEO of the Goldwater Institute, leading the Institute’s efforts to help people in all 50 states live freer, happier lives.

    #30573. Delta CEO’s Cope: Ed Bastian Notes Doesn’t Need Starlink, Current Wi-Fi Good Enough

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 19m • 📚 Deep Dive (3867 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Delta CEO’s Cope: Ed Bastian Notes Doesn’t Need Starlink, Current Wi-Fi Good Enough

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3867 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Delta Air Lines CEO Ed Bastian says “customers are not choosing airlines based on the Wi-Fi.” That’s a remarkable claim from an airline that’s spent years promoting free internet as a reason to choose its premium experience.
    • Speaking at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit on Monday, Bastian defended passing on Starlink and waiting for Amazon Leo which is still unproven and whose timetable is now in question.
    • Industry observers note that it was pure cope.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Delta Air Lines CEO Ed Bastian says “customers are not choosing airlines based on the Wi-Fi.” That’s a remarkable claim from an airline that’s spent years promoting free internet as a reason to choose its premium experience. Speaking at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit on Monday, Bastian defended passing on Starlink and waiting for Amazon Leo which is still unproven and whose timetable is now in question. He downplayed competitors’ progress, argued Delta’s current Viasat service comes close enough, and expressed confidence that Amazon would match or beat Starlink. It was pure cope. Delta doesn’t plan to begin installing Amazon until 2028 and that’s if the service works and delivers on schedule. United and Southwest both plan to finish their Starlink installations in 2027, and American is adding the service as well (so are Alaska and even Frontier). Delta’s Wifi Was Fine When Fewer People Used It Delta’s Viasat internet was fine when a few people on each flight were paying to use it. Make it free, get a much larger share of the plane online, and the experience can become unusable. I wrote about this last December after flying Delta to Las Vegas. The system repeatedly bogged down until nothing would load. I’d rather pay for internet that works than get free internet that doesn’t. Bandwidth has to be shared. Removing the price doesn’t create more capacity, but it gives a lot more people a reason to connect. A connection that works well with light use just isn’t the same thing – and Starlink’s low earth orbit satellites simply give the signal less distance to travel, delivering almost no latency. Bastian points to two fresh Viasat satellites. ViaSat-3 F3 entered service in August, and F2 entered service in September. But Delta’s own current wifi explanation acknowledges that performance varies with customer demand and satellite capacity, with less consistent service in high-demand or capacity-constrained areas. The airline knows this problem exists, which is why they’re touting Amazon’s service as a future improvement. United And Southwest Are Already Flying Starlink Bastian suggests most airlines promoting Starlink haven’t started yet. He doesn’t identify which airlines he’s counting. Here’s what the competitors actually say: United Airlines: More than half its daily flights already have Starlink. It expects nearly 64% by year-end and completion of installations by the end of 2027. Southwest Airlines: Its latest quarterly filing confirms equipped aircraft are already in service, with the full fleet expected to be finished in fall 2027. Last week it publicized gaming and livestreaming aboard a flight from Austin to San Diego. Alaska and Hawaiian: The group’s October 26 installation upgrade indicates all 93 Embraer 175s, Hawaiian’s 18 Airbus A321neos and 24 Airbus A330s equipped, along with 16 Boeing 737 MAX aircraft. Even Southwest expects to have Starlink throughout its fleet before Delta starts putting Amazon on its first 500 aircraft. That’s an awkward comparison for the airline charging a premium when it’ll be universal on the only U.S. airline without first class even. Wifi Doesn’t Have To Decide Every Ticket To Cost Delta Money I explained last month that I’ve avoided United and Southwest when I couldn’t count on functional internet. Starlink changes that calculation. I’ll pay more to work onboard because losing several productive hours costs more than the airfare savings. Recon Analytics finds wifi ranks among the top five business-trip airline selection factors for 32.6% of flyers, and first for 6.5%. Even among leisure travelers, 3.8% rank it first. Delta doesn’t need to lose everyone. It can lose a few expensive trips from customers who fly often, buy premium seats and carry airline credit cards. That’s precisely the business it wants. United is already using wifi to recruit those customers. It says its wifi-focused status match campaign produced a tenfold increase in daily applications. Amazon Still Has To Deliver. Bastian says that when Delta gets Amazon Leo, “we’ll be at least as good as Starlink if not better.” He hasn’t demonstrated that. Amazon needs enough satellites in the right orbits, working aircraft equipment, certification, and an airline installation program. It then has to deliver consistently with actual passengers using it. Delta’s own materials make the 2028 start subject to technical, certification and deployment milestones. And 2028 is the start of installations on an initial 500 aircraft. As I covered yesterday, Sunday’s failed Vulcan launch lost 40 Amazon satellites. We don’t yet know whether that pushes back Delta’s rollout. But the risk extends beyond replacing those satellites: Amazon contracted for 38 Vulcan missions to launch more than 1,500 of them. Amazon’s prelaunch photo shows the satellites stacked for that mission. Bastian’s account of testing Starlink is consistent with reporting from 2022. Delta had an early look at the product. It chose different commercial terms. I’ve covered the dispute over Delta’s branded portal. And last month Bastian said the branding disagreement out loud: “(Elon) thought it should be called Starlink on the planes. I said ‘No, it’s gotta be Delta.’” Amazon could offer a broader deal involving cloud computing and entertainment. Delta also gets to keep directing passengers through its own platform, where it promotes partners and sells them things. But a cheaper contract has to save enough to cover the business lost while passengers wait. If someone moves expensive flights to United, earns status there and starts spending on a United credit card, Delta may have to buy that loyalty back long after Amazon finally arrives.     Van Hollen announces bid for majority leader, but Schumer says he has the votes

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (775 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Chris Van Hollen announced Thursday night that he would run for Senate majority leader, launching a challenge to Sen.
    • Recent findings suggest that van Hollen, a Maryland Democrat first elected to the Senate in 2016, served in leadership in the House and has been chairman of both the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee.
    • Recent findings suggest that “In this election, the American people called for change.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that sen. Chris Van Hollen announced Thursday night that he would run for Senate majority leader, launching a challenge to Sen. Charles E. Schumer of Latest York, the current Democratic leader.

    Recent findings suggest that van Hollen, a Maryland Democrat first elected to the Senate in 2016, served in leadership in the House and has been chairman of both the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. He has said since the midterm elections he was listening to fellow Senate Democrats about the possibility of a run for the top job.

    Recent findings suggest that “In this election, the American people called for change. They called for a change from Donald Trump’s disastrous policies but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn’t working for working people,” Van Hollen mentioned in a statement. “It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need upcoming leadership. This is not about any one person – it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.”.

    Schumer has already said he has the votes needed to continue serving as the leader.

    “I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the vital work ahead. I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together — 55 seats and counting is an amazing result — and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader. I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people,” Schumer said in a statement.

    Industry observers note that schumer's supporters were quick to highlight the success at the ballot box in 2026, with the Democratic caucus potentially growing to 56 seats if former Rep. Mary Peltola prevails in Alaska.

    It has been revealed that “Chuck has outlined an aggressive blueprint for the new Democratic majority which is directly responsive to the message we heard from the voters, and he has the experience and unique mastery of the Senate process to make it happen,” Sen. Angus King, a Maine independent who caucuses with the Democrats, noted in a statement. “Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?”.

    In keeping with the World Series theme, Sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., echoed King with her own statement of support for Schumer.

    “The Brewers just had a record season, and next year is not the time to change our management," Baldwin mentioned. "The same is true in the Senate.”.

    In an interview with MS NOW about his run, Van Hollen conceded that Schumer would be the favorite in the secret-ballot contest, which will take place in December.

    “Am I the underdog? Yes,” Van Hollen said. “You’re talking about an incumbent who uses the power of incumbency to, you know, provide deals to people.”.

    According to recent reports, van Hollen outlined legislative priorities including restoring Medicaid funding that Republicans cut in last year's budget reconciliation law and extending Affordable Care Act tax credits. But he suggested Democrats need to go further.

    According to recent reports, "We need to extend tax credits for the Affordable Care Act, but we can’t stop there, right? We have a completely broken health care system. It’s become profits, not people. And so my view is, we also need in the first 100 days to make health care more affordable for tens of millions of people," Van Hollen said. "We need to immediately make it clear that nobody’s going to pay one penny to subsidize data centers. ... We need to make sure that we have a livable minimum wage.".

    He also said he would not take sides in contested Democratic primaries, and he would make sure the DSCC did not take money from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, or AIPAC.

    It has been revealed that van Hollen's early backers include progressive Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, who emerged from a hotly contested Democratic primary in Michigan while the Senate Democratic political apparatus was backing Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich.

    “In April, I was the first candidate in the country to call on Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead Senate Democrats, and I am proud to stand with him in his bid to become Senate Majority Leader,” El-Sayed noted in a statement. “Michiganders demand money out of politics, money in pockets, and Medicare for All. Sen. Chris Van Hollen offers both the courage to go toe-to-toe with the Trump administration to deliver for working people and the experience to maneuver the Senate caucus. It’s why he has my full support to lead our caucus.”.

    Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that chase and Hyatt have two co-branded credit cards — the World of Hyatt Credit Card (learn more) and World of Hyatt Business Card (learn more).
    • Industry observers note that one of the awesome things about Hyatt’s two credit cards is that they can earn you elite nights, making it easier to qualify for status in the World of Hyatt program.
    • Chase and Hyatt have both the World of Hyatt Credit Card (a personal card) and the World of Hyatt Business Credit Card (a business card).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that chase and Hyatt have two co-branded credit cards — the World of Hyatt Credit Card (learn more) and World of Hyatt Business Card (learn more). I’d consider these to be among the more lucrative hotel credit cards out there, particularly the personal version of the card.

    Industry observers note that one of the awesome things about Hyatt’s two credit cards is that they can earn you elite nights, making it easier to qualify for status in the World of Hyatt program. In this post, I’d like to get into the nitty-gritty of how earning Hyatt elite status with credit cards works, and discuss whether it’s worth it.

    Chase and Hyatt have both the World of Hyatt Credit Card (a personal card) and the World of Hyatt Business Credit Card (a business card). Both cards have valuable benefits, though I think the personal card is considerably more compelling than the business card. Let me start by just briefly recapping the perks of the two cards.

    The World of Hyatt Credit Card has a $95 annual fee and offers:.

    Sources indicate that this means that you’re getting five elite nights toward status and a Category 1-4 free night award every year just for having the card. To me that more than justifies the annual fee, by a long shot (I consistently get $250+ of value out of the free night certificate alone). That doesn’t even factor in the incremental perks you can get for spending on the card.

    The World of Hyatt Business Credit Card has a $199 annual fee and offers:.

    In a recent development, the business version of the card isn’t quite as rewarding as the personal version of the card, especially if you’re not a major spender. However, for businesses that spend quite a bit on credit cards, this can be the best card for earning elite status.

    According to recent reports, both the World of Hyatt Credit Card and World of Hyatt Business Credit Card offer the ability to earn elite nights. However, the ways in which you earn elite nights differ between the two cards, so let’s go over those details.

    The World of Hyatt Credit Card offers qualifying nights toward Hyatt status in two ways. First of all, the World of Hyatt Card offers five elite nights annually just for having the card. There’s no spending required to earn these five elite nights, and you receive them for each calendar year in which you have the card, including the year in which you open the card.

    Beyond that, the World of Hyatt Card offers two elite nights for every $5,000 spent on the card (in other words, that’s up to one elite night per $2,500 of spending). There’s no limit to how many elite nights you can earn this way, and the elite nights earned through spending on this card aren’t in any way tied to the calendar year. In other words, if you spent $2,500 on the card in 2026 and then spend $2,500 on the card in 2027, you’d earn two elite nights at that point.

    The World of Hyatt Business Credit Card offers five elite nights for every $10,000 spent on the card in a calendar year (in other words, that’s up to one elite night per $2,000 of spending). On this card, the spending counter resets at the beginning of the calendar year. In other words, if you spent $8,000 on the card in 2026, you’d still have to spend a full $10,000 in 2027 to earn five elite nights.

    As you can see, this card offers elite nights for spending at an accelerated rate, though unlike the personal card, it doesn’t offer the five elite nights annually just for having the card.

    How soon do elite nights post from the World of Hyatt Credit Card and the World of Hyatt Business Credit Card?

    While the above covers the basics, I’d like to now analyze the overall value proposition of earning World of Hyatt elite status by spending on the World of Hyatt Credit Card or World of Hyatt Business Card, including addressing some of the most common questions and scenarios that come up.

    With Hyatt, not all elite perks are tied directly to having status, but rather some require earning a certain number of elite nights in a year, known as the Milestone Rewards program. The Milestone Rewards program is how you earn perks like suite upgrade awards, club access awards, Guest of Honor awards, and more.

    Hyatt elite nights earned through Hyatt credit cards would count toward Milestone Rewards the same as any hotel stays would, which adds further value to credit card spending.

    Recent findings suggest that one of the perks of both Hyatt credit cards is that you receive Discoverist status for as long as you have the card. Discoverist status ordinarily requires 10 elite qualifying nights or 25,000 base points per year. As a reminder, here are World of Hyatt’s elite thresholds:.

    Sources indicate that one common point of confusion is that people assume these cards really come with up to 15 elite nights per year. They assume you already get Discoverist status, and that any elite nights are on top of that. Note that while these cards offer Discoverist status, you don’t get the elite nights that correspond to that.

    This means that if you have a Hyatt credit card, you’ll receive Discoverist status on an ongoing basis (and five elite nights every year if you have the personal card), but you’ll still need to qualify for Explorist or Globalist status based on the full criteria.

    Sources indicate that hyatt’s lifetime Globalist status is based on earning one million base points in the program. World of Hyatt members earn five base points per dollar spent on Hyatt stays, meaning you essentially have to spend $200,000 at Hyatts to earn lifetime Globalist status.

    Credit card spending, and any elite nights earned through Hyatt credit cards, won’t count toward lifetime Globalist status. That’s because the qualification criteria is based solely on base points, and not based on elite qualifying nights (in which case it would count).

    World of Hyatt Globalist is my favorite top tier hotel status, and what I love is that Hyatt’s co-branded credit cards make it easier to earn that. Let’s look at the best strategy for earning Globalist status with the card. Hyatt Globalist status ordinarily requires earning 60 qualifying nights in a year. So how much would you have to spend on a Hyatt credit card to earn that status?

    On the World of Hyatt Credit Card, you’d need to spend $140,000 to earn Globalist status:.

    Meanwhile on the World of Hyatt Business Credit Card, you’d need to spend $120,000 to earn Globalist status:.

    As you can see, the personal credit card offers more elite nights upfront, while the business credit card offers elite nights at a faster pace for spending (assuming you can reach the thresholds).

    When you’re analyzing the value of spending your way toward status, don’t forget that even beyond the general status perks, the Milestone Rewards perks could really add up. For example, if you make it to 60 elite nights, you could select five suite upgrade awards and four club access awards, and would also receive a Category 1-7 free night award, a Category 1-4 free night award, and three Guest of Honor awards.

    Then on the personal version of the card, you also receive an additional Category 1-4 free night award when you spend $15,000 on the card in a year. The value of all of those perks really adds up.

    Hyatt counts award nights toward status, and just for having the World of Hyatt Credit Card, you get a free night every year, plus the opportunity to earn a further three free nights for spending $15,000, earning Explorist status, and earning Globalist status.

    On top of that, presumably you want to earn Globalist status because you actually intend to stay at Hyatts with some frequency. Hotel status is worthless if you don’t actually stay at that brand.

    It has been revealed that to be realistic, let’s assume that long term you’re earning 30 elite nights per year through actual stays. There are so many great Globalist benefits to use (like suite upgrade awards and free night awards), so if you’re staying at Hyatts less than that I question whether Globalist is worth it for you.

    If you earned 30 of the required 60 elite nights through credit card spending, you’d need to spend the following:.

    Given all the incremental perks you’re picking up with Milestone Rewards, I’d say the math could really check out.

    Industry observers note that when deciding if it makes sense to spend money on the World of Hyatt Credit Card or World of Hyatt Business Credit Card, consider the opportunity cost of the spending. For easy math purposes, I tend to consider the opportunity cost of credit card spending to be around 3.4%.

    That’s because based on my valuation of miles & points, most transferable points currencies are worth 1.7 cents each, and you have some cards offering 2x points per dollar spent. Meanwhile I value World of Hyatt points at 1.4 cents each.

    Recent findings suggest that if we were to theoretically assume you’re spending $60,000 on a Hyatt credit card per year (give or take) in order to earn Globalist status, what’s the opportunity cost of that spending? By my math, you’re looking at an opportunity cost of up to 2% (the spread between a 3.4% return and 1.4% return). That’s around $1,200, if you value things the way that I do. But that’s not factoring in the value of all the other perks mentioned above:.

    For many, I think the above perks could more than justify the difference in return on spending otherwise.

    There are many things to love about the World of Hyatt Credit Card or World of Hyatt Business Card, though the ability to get a fast track toward status is probably my favorite perk. I absolutely love Hyatt Globalist status, and credit cards have historically helped me requalify for status. If you’re a Hyatt loyalist and don’t yet have the hotel group’s co-branded credit cards, they’re seriously worth considering.
