    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Hyatt Credit Card Offer: Earn 4 Free Nights—Why I Spend On The Card Towards Elite Status

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3319 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog.
    • The World Of Hyatt Credit Card (See rates and fees) has a latest initial bonus: earn 4 free nights at any Category 1-4 Hyatt hotel or resort after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening.
    • I have this card, and I put actual spending on it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

    The World Of Hyatt Credit Card (See rates and fees) has a latest initial bonus: earn 4 free nights at any Category 1-4 Hyatt hotel or resort after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. That’s an improved offer from a card whose bonuses have usually been more modest than competing travel cards.

    I have this card, and I put actual spending on it. Hyatt points are still valuable, but what gets me to use the card is the credit toward elite status and the rewards earned along the way. Hyatt status does more to improve my hotel stays than status with other major chains.

    These are four separate certificates, so you can use them for one trip or spread them across different stays. You’ll need standard room award availability, and the certificates expire 12 months after they’re issued. The terms require checkout before the expiration date. Under Hyatt’s current award chart, a Category 4 standard room can cost as much as 25,000 points per night. Four certificates could therefore cover nights that would otherwise require 100,000 points. Their category restrictions and expiration date make them less flexible than having those points in your account. The card has a $95 annual fee. Chase excludes current holders of this card and previous cardmembers who received its initial bonus within the past 24 months. The usual Chase restriction on applicants who’ve opened five or more personal cards in the past 24 months also generally applies. Why I Keep The Card And Spend On It The annual Category 1-4 free night after each cardmember anniversary makes the $95 fee easy to justify. There’s also a second Category 1-4 night after $15,000 in purchases during a calendar year which makes that spending more rewarding. And these nights are transferable to another World of Hyatt member. If I won’t use one, I can give it to someone who will. For spending, the card earns 4 Hyatt points per dollar on qualifying Hyatt purchases; 2 on restaurants, airline tickets bought directly from airlines, local transit and commuting, and fitness club and gym memberships; and 1 on other purchases. More significantly, it comes with 5 qualifying nights each year, plus 2 more qualifying nights for every $5,000 spent. Those nights count toward both status and Milestone Rewards. Put $15,000 of otherwise unbonused spending on the card during a calendar year and you earn: 15,000 Hyatt points. An additional Category 1-4 free night certificate. 6 qualifying nights from spending, giving you 11 including the card’s annual 5. That means 49 qualifying nights actually spent in hotels, plus the card’s 5 annual nights and 6 from spending, gets you to the 60 needed for Globalist. And the $5,000 spent earning the initial bonus counts toward the $15,000 free-night threshold in the calendar year when you spend it. Milestone Rewards start at 20 qualifying nights and continue every 10 nights through 150. Some of the rewards on the way to Globalist are: Qualifying Nights Notable Rewards 30 A Category 1-4 free night, plus a choice of additional reward. 40 A Guest of Honor Award, plus a choice that includes a Suite Upgrade Award. 50 A choice that includes 2 Suite Upgrade Awards. 60 Globalist status, a Category 1-7 free night, 2 Suite Upgrade Awards, 2 Guest of Honor Awards, and My Hyatt Concierge. The value of another $5,000 in spending depends on where those two nights get me. Crossing a threshold for suite upgrades or Globalist can be worth giving up a higher earning rate on another card. Hyatt Status Is Stronger Than At Other Major Chains The card itself comes with Discoverist status. That’s better than a hole in the head as my grandfather used to say. But reaching Globalist has real value – as well as the milestone choices along the way. The biggest benefit is confirming a suite at the time of booking with a Suite Upgrade Award for up to seven nights when an eligible standard suite is available for the stay. That’s a huge value on family trips. I also value having a My Hyatt Concierge I can email requests to, actual delivery of 4 p.m. late checkout at eligible properties, and a more generous breakfast benefit than I get from other chains. At participating hotels without an available club lounge, Globalist breakfast generally covers a full breakfast for up to two adults and two children registered in the room, including tax and gratuity. Late checkout has exceptions, including availability limits at resorts, but I’m usually proactively offered late checkout everywhere else (and personally find it honored more often than not at resorts). The Free Night Certificates Should Be More Flexible The current version of this card launched in 2018. Its annual certificate is still capped at Category 4, while category creep has taken away many of the hotels where I’d most want to use it. Just this year, 14 hotels moved from Category 4 to Category 5, including Hyatt Regency Seattle, Hyatt Regency Grand Cypress and Hyatt Regency Jersey City. Five moved the other way, bringing options like Hyatt Centric Congress Avenue Austin and Dream Nashville within reach, but the certificate lost more hotels than it gained. I’d like Hyatt to at least let members add points to a certificate to book a higher category. The certificate works at a Category 4 hotel charging 25,000 points, but won’t work at a Category 5 hotel when it’s charging 15,000 points. And I wish Hyatt would let us combine these free nights with Suite Upgrade Awards or Guest of Honor Awards. I value them most traveling with my family when I’m paying for rooms out of pocket. That’s always when I want to use my suite upgrades! I don’t need a suite on a business stay (paid by someone else, when it’s just me) or to use the free night award.     #30556. Delta SkyMiles Blue Amex Review: Is The No Annual Fee Card Worth It?

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2124 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    Delta SkyMiles Blue Amex Review: Is The No Annual Fee Card Worth It?

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2124 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • American Express and Delta have had a close relationship for many years, and as part of that, they matter seven co-branded Delta Amex cards.
    • Link: Learn more about the Delta SkyMiles® Blue American Express Card.
    • Before I get into the full Delta Blue Amex Card review, here’s an overview of the card’s main features, from its welcome bonus and earning rates, to other benefits:.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    American Express and Delta have had a close relationship for many years, and as part of that, they matter seven co-branded Delta Amex cards. This is my in-depth Delta SkyMiles® Blue American Express Card review, as this is the entry-level personal Delta credit card with no annual fee (Rates & Fees), and probably the least talked about card in the lineup. It’s far from the most rewarding Delta credit card, but if you want to earn Delta miles and only fly the airline occasionally, it could be worth a look.

    Link: Learn more about the Delta SkyMiles® Blue American Express Card.

    Before I get into the full Delta Blue Amex Card review, here’s an overview of the card’s main features, from its welcome bonus and earning rates, to other benefits:.

    Beyond that, here are my thoughts on the pros and cons of the Delta Blue Amex:.

    Industry observers note that when applying for a credit card, the welcome bonus, eligibility rules, and fees, are obviously major factors that people consider. With that in mind, let’s take a look at those details for the Delta Blue Amex Card. As you’d expect for this card, the lack of fees largely comes at expense of a smaller welcome offer.

    In a recent development, the Blue Delta SkyMiles Amex has a welcome offer of 10,000 bonus SkyMiles after spending $1,000 within the first six months of your card membership. Based on my latest points & miles valuations, Delta SkyMiles are worth 1.1 cents each, making this bonus worth $110. We’ve seen this card’s bonus go a bit higher, but not by a huge amount.

    Sources indicate that the bonuses on all other Delta Amex cards are significantly higher, which isn’t a surprise, since cards with annual fees often have better bonuses than cards without annual fees. It’s hard to get excited about that offer, but I guess something is better than nothing?

    The welcome offer on the Delta Blue Amex Card is “once in a lifetime,” so it’s not available to you if you currently have the card, or if you’ve had the card in the past. The rules go beyond that, though.

    You’re actually not eligible for the bonus on the card if you have or have had any of the more premium versions of the Delta Amex card portfolio, at least among the personal cards. This is true across the portfolio, and the idea is that you’re always eligible for the bonus on a more premium card, but not eligible for the bonus on a less premium card.

    So if you do want to pick up multiple Delta Amex cards, you’ll want to first apply for the Delta Blue Amex, then the Delta Gold Amex, then the Delta Platinum Amex, and then the Delta Reserve Amex (or at least you’ll want to move in that general order).

    Beyond that, Amex’s general card application restrictions apply, including that you can typically have at most five credit cards from Amex at a time (that doesn’t include hybrid cards).

    In a recent development, let me emphasize once again that the Blue Delta Amex has no annual fee. It’s great to see a trend whereby we’re seeing more airline credit cards with no annual fees, since it’s a nice option for someone who wants a co-branded credit card, but doesn’t want to pay an annual fee.

    You can also add additional people to the card at no extra cost.

    According to recent reports, there’s no doubt that card issuers are moving toward offering more no annual fee cards with no foreign transaction fees, though it’s still not the standard. The Blue Delta Amex has no foreign transaction fees (Rates & Fees), which is awesome, since most Amex no annual fee cards do still have these fees.

    When it comes to earning rewards, the Blue Delta SkyMiles Credit Card offers:.

    For a no annual fee product, it’s nice to see a card offering a bonus on dining. While some bonus categories are better than none, I don’t find the bonuses to be particularly compelling, as there are still better cards out there for airfare purchases and restaurant purchases.

    Industry observers note that while Delta SkyMiles is far from my favorite mileage currency, it does have a high floor value, so there are good ways to redeem Delta SkyMiles. You can redeem SkyMiles for flights on Delta or on Delta’s SkyTeam partners, like Air France, China Airlines, and Korean Air.

    According to recent reports, partner award flights can be an especially good option if you focus on flights that don’t touch the United States, since flights that do are more expensive and get you less value for your miles. I’ve also seen some good award prices for Delta One (business class) awards, specifically for booking roundtrip rather than one way.

    The Delta Blue Amex is a decent no annual fee card in the sense that it offers 2x miles at restaurants and has no foreign transaction fees, but how are the perks on the card? Not surprisingly, this is an area where the card lags, and where the cards with annual fees offer significantly more value.

    Nonetheless, there are some perks to the card that may prove valuable to the occasional Delta flyer.

    Sources indicate that if you have the Blue Delta Amex, then you can save 20% in the form of a statement credit for eligible pre-purchased meals, and in-flight purchases of food or alcoholic beverages, on Delta flights. Allow 8-12 weeks for the statement credit to post.

    Having the Blue Delta Amex makes you eligible for the Delta Pay With Miles program. What is that? This allows those with co-branded Delta Amex cards to redeem miles for one cent each towards a Delta flight purchase (in increments of 5,000 miles per $50). That’s not the best deal in the world, though this is a feature that’s exclusively available to those with an eligible card.

    Some people find this to be useful since they can redeem their miles towards flights, and then they still earn elite miles for taking those flights.

    In other words, the 10,000 miles available as part of the welcome offer can be redeemed for a minimum of $100 worth of travel on Delta. This is obviously the lowest cost option for unlocking that benefit.

    According to recent reports, the Delta Blue Amex includes access to dedicated entrance lanes and fast lanes at stadiums and arenas that participate in the Amex Venue Collection program. As part of this benefit, you can also get 10% back on qualifying concessions purchases, up to $250 back per calendar year. (Enrollment required).

    Industry observers note that amex Offers is a program that offers discounts for purchases with all kinds of retailers. There’s huge value to be had in getting as many Amex cards as possible, so that you can get these offers on multiple cards.

    The ideal situation is to have a no annual fee card (like this one), so you can get access to these offers without paying an annual fee to get access to this.

    Amex Offers could save you hundreds of dollars per year. You can access these offers by logging into your account and scrolling down to the bottom of your account summary page.

    The Delta Blue Amex comes with some basic travel and purchase protection benefits:.

    There are some coverage limits and exclusions to be aware of, so you’ll want to review the full details in the card’s benefits guide before assuming you’re insured.

    According to recent reports, car rental loss and damage insurance: Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Tech giant. Car Rental Loss or Damage Coverage is offered through American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc. Extended warranty and purchase protection: Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company.

    Many people who like Delta as a brand may be tempted to pick up the Delta Blue Amex — it allows you to earn miles with Delta, it has no annual fee, and it offers some perks that could add value (20% off inflight purchases, Amex Offers, access to Delta Pay With Miles, etc.).

    However, in general, I wouldn’t recommend outright applying for this card:.

    Let me address both of those points below.

    If you’re considering the Delta SkyMiles Blue Amex, let me make the case for applying for the Delta SkyMiles® Gold American Express Card (learn more) instead, which right now has the limited-time offer:.

    According to recent reports, you can always get the Gold Delta Amex, and then if you don’t find it to be worth the annual fee, you can downgrade it to the Blue Delta Amex after a year. That would allow you to maintain the card account, and you wouldn’t pay the annual fee when you downgrade (and you’d still get the elevated perks and bigger bonus for the first year).

    At a minimum, it really is worth trying the Delta Gold Amex to see if you like it and to take advantage of the better bonus, and then you can downgrade at a later point if you find it’s not worthwhile.

    If you are looking to earn Delta SkyMiles through credit card spending then consider using a card earning Amex Membership Rewards points. That’s because these points can be transferred to Delta SkyMiles at a 1:1 ratio, and you can in many cases earn points at a much faster rate.

    Sources indicate that for example, the American Express® Gold Card (learn more) offers 4x points at restaurants worldwide (on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year and then 1x) and at U.S. supermarkets (on up to $25,000 in purchases per calendar year and then 1x), and 3x points on flights booked directly with airlines or at AmexTravel.com. That’s a much better return than you’ll get on this card, and it’s also quite easy to make the math on the card work.

    If you’re absolutely committed to having a no annual fee card and want to maximize your return on spending, there are lots of excellent no annual fee cards to consider.

    According to recent reports, my favorite is the Citi Double Cash® Card (learn more). The card earns 1% cash back when you make a purchase, and 1% cash back when you pay for that purchase (in the form of ThankYou points).

    But it gets even better than that — rewards earned on this card can be converted into ThankYou points at a 1:1 ratio and can be moved to partner programs at the best possible ratio, assuming you have the card in conjunction with one earning premium ThankYou points, like the Citi Strata Premier® Card (learn more).

    That means the card earns two ThankYou points per dollar, and I value those points at 1.7 cents each, so that’s like a 3.4% return on everyday spending.

    Sources indicate that I appreciate that American Express and Delta offer a no annual fee option with the Delta Blue Amex. For someone absolutely committed to getting a Delta Amex Card and not paying an annual fee, this is the best/only option.

    The card has no foreign transaction fees, offers 2x miles on dining, and gives you access to Pay With Miles and 20% discounts on inflight purchases.

    Industry observers note that however, for most people, I think it’s worth applying for the Delta Gold Amex. The card has a lot more perks and a much better bonus, and you can always downgrade the card to the Delta Blue Amex after at least a year.

    The day after the Democrats trounced the Republicans in the midterm elections, Ezra Klein of the Upcoming York Times tweeted, “One of the more exciting parts of this election — among many — is the return of a religious left.” Accompanying the enthusiastic remark was a clip from his interview earlier this year with James Talarico, the Democrat who won the Texas senatorial race. In the clip, Talarico — a Presbyterian seminarian — advocates a political attitude in which Americans recognize each other as being made in God’s image and treat each other accordingly. He calls this “an incarnational politics.”.

    Recent findings suggest that incarnational politics — hoo boy. The term, a nearly paradoxical union of the sacred and the profane, sounds just enough like intersectional politics to catch the attention of progressives. It also sounds like an edgy indie band that never quite made it. (“I saw Incarnational Politics open for Bad Religion in ’91.”).

    Christopher J. Scalia is a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute and the author of 13 Novels Conservatives Will Love (but Probably Haven’t Read).

    • Three women stranded in Charlotte after Friday’s nationwide flight grounding bought a $48,000 Ford Bronco and drove 27 hours home to North Dakota.
    • Tara Harding (I first read this as Tonya Harding) and two employees needed to get back to their families in Bismarck, and had patients to see Monday morning.
    • Tara Harding and her employees were at the airport trying to get home from a work trip when a nationwide ground stop left them stranded in Charlotte, North Carolina — roughly 1,600 miles from home in Bismarck, North Dakota.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Three women stranded in Charlotte after Friday’s nationwide flight grounding bought a $48,000 Ford Bronco and drove 27 hours home to North Dakota. They’d gone away for work training. They came home with a fresh car. Tara Harding (I first read this as Tonya Harding) and two employees needed to get back to their families in Bismarck, and had patients to see Monday morning. Tara Harding and her employees were at the airport trying to get home from a work trip when a nationwide ground stop left them stranded in Charlotte, North Carolina — roughly 1,600 miles from home in Bismarck, North Dakota. She found a $48,000 solution in the form of a new Ford Bronco. https://t.co/xpP9fmCsm8 — NBC News (@NBCNews) November 16, 2026 They couldn’t find a rental car within four hours of Charlotte. They tried other ways home, including a train, bus and U-Haul. None worked. Delta Air Lines left them stranded. Harding’s mother-in-law suggested buying a car. They bought the Bronco with no money down. Harding initially planned to sell it to a dealership once they reached home. The women took turns driving and sleeping. While flights resumed at 8:15 p.m. Eastern on Friday, over 18,000 trips were cancelled and there simply weren’t seats to accommodate all passengers on later flights and it took several days to clear everyone out. There’s a calculation in buying the car, deducting depreciation, taxes and fees, financing costs and operating expenses, and selling it on the other end. There’s a very close precedent. During Southwest Airlines’ Christmas 2022 meltdown, a couple bought a $500 used car to get home, and Southwest reimbursed them. This incident wasn’t any airline’s fault. In the end, Harding abandoned the strategy to resell the car.     Surprise: Aer Lingus Unveils First-Ever Premium Economy, Coming To 10 A330s

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (759 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that aer Lingus is getting on the premium economy hype.
    • This is quite a big change, and one that should give it a leg up in the highly competitive trans-Atlantic market.
    • According to recent reports, the cabin will feature just four rows with 28 seats in a 2-3-2 configuration.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that aer Lingus is getting on the premium economy hype. The Irish flag carrier has today revealed it will introduce the cabin for the first time on 10 of its Airbus A330s, which will also feature new business and economy cabins (the product won’t be coming to the Airbus A321LR/XLR fleet).

    This is quite a big change, and one that should give it a leg up in the highly competitive trans-Atlantic market.

    According to recent reports, the cabin will feature just four rows with 28 seats in a 2-3-2 configuration. That’s about average when compared to other premium economy cabins. The narrow fuselage of the A330 means there’s only room for three seats in the middle section, rather than the four many other airlines offer.

    In terms of specs, the 18-19 inch wide Recaro R4 seats will offer 38 inches of pitch and eight inches of recline. In addition to footrests, a staple of any decent premium economy, the seats have been designed with fixed headrest wings to provide a sense of privacy.

    As for the soft product, Aer Lingus promises three-course dining, drinks throughout the flight, a pillow and blanket, an amenity kit, and noise-reducing (not noise-canceling) headphones.

    Sources indicate that I actually really like the design and color scheme. It’s modern, looks elegant and premium, and most importantly of all for the airline of the Emerald Isle, the colors are quintessentially Irish.

    Aer Lingus says premium economy fares will start from 700 Euros one-way, putting a return trip at around 1,400 Euros. That works out to around $1,534, and a few hundred dollars cheaper than United’s nonstop fares from Newark (EWR) to Dublin (DUB).

    It has been revealed that we’ll have to wait until October 1 next year to try Aer Lingus’ new premium economy out for ourselves. The airline hasn’t yet announced which routes will get the product first, but we should find out in the coming months.

    The good news is, they’ll operate on many of the airline’s 18 nonstop routes from Dublin to the United States.

    As a small, almost boutique-style airline with just 63 aircraft, Aer Lingus must remain competitive, especially in the saturated transatlantic market in which it predominantly operates. The addition of premium economy bridges the large gap between economy and business, and should open the airline up to a potential new customer base who’ve never flown it before.

    I’ll be attending an event in Dublin tonight, so I should be back with more images and extra info soon!

    What do you make of Aer Lingus’ upcoming premium economy?

    #30551. Industry News: 45-Minute Immigration Queues & $25 Airport Meals: My Experience Flying Through Vietnam's Overcrowded Airport

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1647 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: 45-Minute Immigration Queues & $25 Airport Meals: My Experience Flying Through Vietnam's Overcrowded Airport

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1647 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that vietnam's Ho Chi Minh International Airport (officially Tan Son Nhat International Airport) is the airport serving Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) and southern Vietnam.
    • Sources indicate that I have lived in Vietnam (a few minutes' drive from the airport) for more than two years, and I regularly fly through it on both international and domestic flights.
    • However, the airport is over capacity and cannot accommodate future growth.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that vietnam's Ho Chi Minh International Airport (officially Tan Son Nhat International Airport) is the airport serving Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) and southern Vietnam. Its passenger volume has grown to the point where it is considerably over capacity, and the international terminal is struggling.

    Sources indicate that I have lived in Vietnam (a few minutes' drive from the airport) for more than two years, and I regularly fly through it on both international and domestic flights. My gym offers a view of aircraft taking off and landing. For me, the convenient proximity of the airport is worth much more than the modernity of the soon-to-open Long Thanh International Airport located well outside the city.

    However, the airport is over capacity and cannot accommodate future growth. The existing terminal was built to handle 8-10 million passengers a year and was expanded to 13 million a year in 2018. Currently, the terminal is handling 18+ million passengers annually. The new airport being constructed (expected to open at the end of 2026 or early 2027) is to complement, but not entirely replace, Tan Son Nhat International Airport.

    Sources indicate that terminal 2 is the international terminal. Domestic services use Terminal 1 and Terminal 3 (more on them below). From my experience, Terminal 2 has enough boarding gates to serve its international flights, although the low-cost airline, VietJet, uses airport shuttle buses. Overall, the terminal is old, somewhat cramped, and run-down.

    Industry observers note that meanwhile, many of its vendors feel more like ad hoc street vendors than modern international airport vendors. I have seen the check-in queues for VietJet wrap around much of the area with wait times of at least an hour. Sometimes VietJet's queues are modest, but they are highly variable. Those flying with VietJet should arrive at the airport sooner.

    Industry observers note that the check-in queues for other airlines are generally fine, with VietJet being a major outlier. Besides VietJet, the airport's major bottleneck is immigration (emigration). As a rule of thumb, the queues for checking in for Vietnam Airlines, AirAsia, and international flag carriers are modest or otherwise acceptable.

    After immigration, the queues for security are relatively better, but it can still take another 15 minutes. Altogether, I consider the terminal to be old, prone to significant queues at immigration, strained, but also perfectly functional. Even under strain, with a single runway, the terminal operates smoothly, and flights are not normally delayed.

    Once past immigration, prices are listed in US dollars, and everything feels overpriced relative to the state of the terminal and the presentation of the vendors. It is common to see the same Vietnamese noodle soup (Pho) that costs the equivalent of $3 outside the airport cost around $25 inside it.

    I'm anticipating that the vendors will be one of the biggest changes at the upcoming Long Thanh International Airport. Most of the vendors sell Vietnamese souvenirs such as traditional conical hats, figurines, Vietnamese coffee, and Vietnamese chocolate. The airport does have a duty-free section, but it is relatively limited.

    Capacity and forecasts of HCMC's twin airports (per Tuoi Tre News).

    13 million (international terminal only).

    50 million (combined terminals, current, to be expanded).

    Up to 100 million (planned, eventual).

    40 million passengers (mostly domestic).

    44.5 million passengers (mostly international).

    50 million passengers (mostly domestic).

    77.5 million passengers (mostly international).

    Separately, when arriving, there is also a relatively modest duty-free section at the baggage reclaim area. The waiting area of the airport is functional, but dated and limited in options. There are dining options offering a selection of Western and Vietnamese food, some lounges, and cafes.

    Industry observers note that one upshot is that the terminal's windows and main dining area have excellent views of the runway and airplane operations. Many of the stock photos used by Simple Flying's articles are from Shutterstock, and a meaningful percentage of these were taken by plane spotters at Tan Son Nhat International Airport​​​​.

    Recent findings suggest that generally, all the immigration and emigration booths are manned all the time. I have never had any concerns with immigration, nor have I seen other passengers having issues. That remarked, I did talk to one Azeri father of several children who said he shouted at the Vietnamese immigration officers until his voice was hoarse.

    It has been revealed that as I recall, his distress was due to immigration refusing entry to his daughter on account of a spelling error on her visa. They eventually let her through. I have passed through Vietnamese land and air checkpoints dozens of times with no concerns. The queue for emigration is commonly 45 minutes. This can be less, but it can also be more, with queues lasting an hour.

    There are some e-Gates, but generally no one, apart from flight crew, seems to use them. I understand there is a fee to use them, but I'm not exactly sure. Unlike most countries, Vietnamese immigration and emigration at this airport do not have separate lines for citizens and foreigners. Having dual nationality, I can choose to visit Vietnam on a British or Latest Zealand passport.

    Vietnam is visa-free for British citizens and most of Europe. US, NZ, Australia, and most others can get a straightforward 90-day eVisa. As a note of caution, there are many third-party websites online offering Vietnamese eVisas. Sometimes these can be faster than going through the official site, but it is important to remember these are not official sites. Bring a printed copy of the eVisa.

    In a recent development, vietnam now requires visitors to fill out the online arrival card. The queues at immigration are around the same as those at emigration. It routinely takes around 45 minutes to get through immigration, with 20 minutes being impressive. An hour is common, depending on how many flights have arrived. All the booths are typically staffed. Arriving passengers can purchase a hassle-free local SIM card before immigration or after customs.

    After immigration and collecting baggage is customs. As of the time of writing, Vietnam does not require a customs declaration form, and it's somewhat random as to whether arrivals need to go through the queue to scan baggage or just walk through the Nothing to Declare line. Plenty of taxis are waiting outside customs. Passengers can book a taxi, or go by e-hailing (Grab is popular).

    Recent findings suggest that there are also currency exchange booths for those wanting Vietnamese Dong. In my experience, Vietnam's ACB bank has the lowest cash withdrawal fees: for me, it's the only bank I've found that is free for international withdrawals. Taxis typically need to be paid in cash (or QR code for those with a Vietnamese bank). The e-hailing app Grab accepts international credit cards, but others may not.

    According to recent reports, the airport has two domestic terminals. Vietnam's low-cost carrier, VietJet, uses the old Terminal 1, while the flag carrier, Vietnam Airlines, has moved operations to the recently opened Terminal 2 (along with Bamboo Airways, Pacific Airlines, Vasco, Sun PhuQuoc Airways). This has freed up capacity in Terminal 1.

    When I've flown through Terminal 1, VietJet was not making use of the extra capacity and check-in counters, meaning queues were as long and frustrating as ever, with terminal capacity idle. Some of the terminal's security capacity was also not in use, resulting in more queues.

    Terminal 3 is the opposite. It is a modern, gleaming latest terminal with plenty of capacity, bright lighting, large windows, and modern vendors. Vietnam is considering looks to continue to expand and upgrade the terminal with more technology. The security check is rapid, and checking in is straightforward.

    Recent findings suggest that getting between the three terminals is a short five-minute, mostly covered walk between Terminal 2 (the international terminal) and Terminal 1 (VietJet's domestic terminal). However, Terminal 3 is isolated and cannot be reached on foot or within the airport itself. There is a free airport shuttle connecting them, or passengers can take taxis.

    Industry observers note that the routes taken are through dense parts of the city and take around 10–15 minutes. Vietnam is presently considering building a tunnel to connect the two domestic terminals. Passengers flying with VietJet should proposal for more time at check-in and security than those flying with Vietnam Airlines.

    Ho Chi Minh City is soon to join other megacities in operating a two-airport system: Mumbai and Bangkok are other notable Asian examples of such cities. When the newly introduced airport, Long Thanh International Airport, opens, it will take over long-haul international operations. However, the old airport will continue operating as a domestic and regional international airport.

    Vietnam Airlines has its new terminal for domestic flights, and there are renovation aims for VietJet's rundown domestic terminal. Proposals will see Terminal 1 demolished and rebuilt, as well as the international terminal upgraded and Terminal 3 progressively expanded. Several rail and road links are being built or expanded to connect the two Ho Chi Minh City airports.

    Sources indicate that work is underway to build the Thu Thiem – Long Thanh Railway to the newly introduced airport. Construction started in July 2026. Thu Thiem is still a considerable distance across the densest parts of the city, so it will improve connectivity, but not directly connect the airports. Meanwhile, future metro lines are expected to reach the original airport in the future. Authorities are discussing a direct highway link, but that is in the early planning stages.

    According to recent reports, ​​​​​​​Until then, the connection between the airports will likely be an concern. Tan Son Nhat is expected to remain a regional international airport, mostly for Southeast Asia destinations. Overall, its traffic is expected to increase to around 40 million annually by 2030, with domestic passengers accounting for around 75% of the total. By that time, Long Thanh should be handling around 45 million passengers annually.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: How Marriott Members Can Sometimes Earn Points Twice On The Same Spending

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1089 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A Marriott Bonvoy member reports earning qualifying spend or extra points by charging gift card purchases to the room bill even though Marriott expressly excludes gift card purchases from the spending requirement for Ambassador status.
    • Ambassador takes 100 qualifying nights and $23,000 in annual qualifying spend.
    • An April 4 report on US Card Forum laid out some properties where this worked, and where it didn’t.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A Marriott Bonvoy member reports earning qualifying spend or extra points by charging gift card purchases to the room bill even though Marriott expressly excludes gift card purchases from the spending requirement for Ambassador status. Ambassador takes 100 qualifying nights and $23,000 in annual qualifying spend. Someone staying at inexpensive and even moderately-priced hotels can clear the nights while falling well short on dollars. If a gift card counts when you buy it, you could move future hotel spending into the current qualification year. And if the purchase and the eventual hotel stay both earn points, you’ve earned twice on the same money. An April 4 report on US Card Forum laid out some properties where this worked, and where it didn’t. Property   Reported result Ritz-Carlton Waikiki spa   Gift cards charged to the room counted toward qualifying spend. St. Regis Longboat Key   Two $1,500 cards purchased, then used at checkout; the member reports an extra round of points. Tampa EDITION   Allowed the gift-card room charge; no separate points or spending total supplied. JW Marriott Clearwater   Refused to put the purchase on the room bill. Unnamed hotel, separate commenter   A charge labeled “gc” reached the folio but earned no points. Marriott’s terms (section 4.2.b.v) exclude Marriott Gift Card purchases from Annual Qualifying Spend. The Ambassador help page says the same thing. This comes down to how the hotel records the charge and sends it to Marriott. If a gift card sale goes through as an eligible incidental, the loyalty system credits the amount without recognizing what was actually sold. A properly identified gift card entry gets excluded. There are two places this can fail: the hotel can refuse the room charge, or accept it but keep it out of the amount eligible for points and status. An employee saying “yes, we can charge that to your room” doesn’t tell you whether it will post as eligible spend. I’ve covered another example of hotel level accounting producing more Ambassador credit than you’d expect. In 2024, the Renaissance Dallas advertised a rate with 30% additional qualifying spend for $20 extra per night. That suggested how the property’s handling of a charge can affect the way Marriott credits it. If you’re a Marriott person, who’s going to spend money with them anyway (clearly an Ambassador member does) this is an interesting thing to experiment with but I also wouldn’t hit it too hard with an Ambassador account that I valued. Me, I haven’t been an Ambassador since the end of the Starwood days.     #30549. Bipartisan process for picking GAO chief breaks down

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (916 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Bipartisan process for picking GAO chief breaks down

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (916 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Republican leaders have skipped a bipartisan deliberative process for recommending the next comptroller general to head the Government Accountability Office, as lawmakers prepare to consider a nomination for the post from President Donald Trump.
    • According to recent reports, sources said Trump is planning to nominate Eric Ueland, who currently serves as deputy director for management at the Office of Management and Budget.
    • Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., on Thursday posted notice of a committee hearing Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Republican leaders have skipped a bipartisan deliberative process for recommending the next comptroller general to head the Government Accountability Office, as lawmakers prepare to consider a nomination for the post from President Donald Trump.

    According to recent reports, sources said Trump is planning to nominate Eric Ueland, who currently serves as deputy director for management at the Office of Management and Budget. The White House submitted ethics paperwork on Ueland — required for nominations — to the GAO, according to a source.

    Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., on Thursday posted notice of a committee hearing Nov. 19 to examine more than a dozen presidential nominees for executive and judicial offices, including “a nominee to be Comptroller General.”.

    The post identifies by name all of the nominees except the candidate for comptroller general. The post has been filled by an acting comptroller general, Orice Williams Brown, since Gene L. Dodaro completed his 15-year term at the end of last year.

    The move by Paul to short-circuit the convening of a legislative commission to recommend candidates infuriated top Democrats, who excoriated the chairman in a joint statement Wednesday night. A special bipartisan, bicameral legislative commission is supposed to recommend at least three candidates for comptroller general to the president, according to statute.

    In a recent development, homeland Security Committee GOP staff solicited recommendations for a comptroller general from some Democratic congressional offices Wednesday afternoon, imposing a deadline of 8 a.m. Thursday, according to Democratic aides.

    The president nominates the head of the GAO, the investigative arm of Congress, with the advice and consent of the Senate.

    Paul pushed back on the criticism Thursday, saying, “Democrats have known about this for months and months and months.” He remarked the last time the special commission made recommendations for the office, when Barack Obama was president, “Democrats submitted their own list, Republicans submitted their own list. So they can complain all they want but they just need to make their list and submit it.”.

    In the past, however, the special commission convened, sought applications for the position, interviewed candidates and deliberated before sending recommendations to the president.

    A 1980 law states that when there is a vacancy in the comptroller general position, “there is established a commission to recommend individuals to the President for appointment to the vacant office,” and that the commission must submit at least three names.

    Under the statute, the commission includes the speaker, Senate majority and minority leaders, House majority and minority leaders, chairs and ranking members of the Senate Homeland Security and House Oversight and Government Reform committees, and the Senate president pro tempore.

    Recent findings suggest that in 1981, for example, after the law took effect, the two congressional leaders, Speaker Thomas P. “Tip” O’Neill Jr., D-Mass., and Senate Majority Leader Howard H. Baker, R-Tenn., sent a letter to President Ronald Reagan saying the special commission had met and voted to recommend eight candidates to succeed Comptroller General Elmer Staats.

    “The members of the Commission have taken their statutory responsibility seriously,” they wrote.

    It has been revealed that reagan nominated Charles A. Bowsher, who was on the list, and he was confirmed.

    According to recent reports, after Bowsher’s term ended in 1996, the commission eventually formed, interviewed multiple candidates, and deliberated for several months. Republicans controlled both chambers, and Bill Clinton was president. The members of the commission could not reach agreement, and as a result, the Republicans on the committee submitted their list to Clinton, and the Democrats on the panel submitted theirs.

    Clinton also had his own list. Clinton nominated David M. Walker, who was on all three lists, and he was confirmed by the Senate more than two years after Bowsher’s departure. Walker argued Thursday against short-circuiting the commission process.

    “The position is of critical importance and the related statutory Commission process should not be circumvented," Walker noted. "Doing so would undercut the credibility of the person and the effectiveness of the GAO.”.

    Walker resigned in March of 2008, when George W. Bush was still president. He appointed Dodaro as acting comptroller general when he left. The commission got going several months later, creating a website with application instructions and candidate questions.

    Over the next two years, the commission interviewed some 20 candidates. Democrats and Republicans on the panel were unable to reach agreement, and Democrats, who had a majority on the commission, submitted their own list to Obama in 2010. Republicans followed up with their list.

    “The Commission has been working in earnest on this undertaking for more than one year and has dedicated considerable time and effort to present you with highly qualified candidates for this important position,” then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., and then-Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid, D-Nev., along with other Democratic leaders, wrote to Obama when they submitted the Democrats’ list.

    According to recent reports, the Democrats’ move drew a rebuke from Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, who was ranking member of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee at the time.

    Recent findings suggest that collins said in a statement she was “extremely disappointed” that Democrats “abruptly ended the selection process for the next Comptroller General without a bipartisan agreement” on the recommendations. “We have had several exceptionally qualified individuals apply to be the next leader of the GAO, and it should have been possible to come up with a consensus list.”.

    Obama nominated and the Senate confirmed Dodaro, who was one of four recommendations from the Democrats.

    • Aer Lingus opted for its take on the ever-popular Collins Elevation suite.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It’s not just Aer Lingus’ premium economy stealing the headlines in Ireland today. Expected to fly passengers for the first time on October 1, 2027, the newly introduced cabins are part of a comprehensive Airbus A330 tip-to-tail retrofit that will include new business and economy cabins. We covered the premium economy cabin in a separate article story.

    Recent findings suggest that the same 10 Airbus A330s that will get the airline’s new premium economy will also get a swanky new business class. The airline’s Airbus A321XLRs aren’t included in this cabin upgrade.

    Aer Lingus opted for its take on the ever-popular Collins Elevation suite. There’ll be 28 seats in a 1-2-1 configuration that stretch out to 78 inches long when in lie-flat mode.

    According to recent reports, the color palette of Irish greens, whites, and light wood gives the seat an elegant yet distinctly non-corporate feel. It’s a thumbs-up from me.

    In a recent development, in terms of updated tech, each seat has 4K HD screens (in all cabins) as well as wireless and USB-C charging. While nothing revolutionary, these touches will significantly modernize Aer Lingus A330 cabins.

    Sources indicate that aer Lingus is also introducing a self-service bar stocked with snacks and drinks. I wonder if this will include Champagne….

    The airline will also serve up a whole new in-flight dining experience featuring dishes inspired by both Irish ingredients and its transatlantic destinations.

    It wouldn’t be a full retrofit without sprucing up economy.

    It has been revealed that per the renderings, Aer Lingus has done a great job again with the cabin’s look and feel. The emerald green Shamrocks are a lovely touch.

    Seats are configured in the A330’s classic 2-4-2 configuration — a favorite for those traveling in pairs.

    While the recline looks a bit modest here, the seat’s thickness looks like it’ll provide more support than some of those ultra-thin, rigid seats airlines are sneaking in these days.

    The six-way adjustable headrests should also mean less head-wobbling when catching some shut-eye.

    The curved design of the seat backs should hopefully mean noticeably more knee space.

    In a recent development, aer Lingus is also upping its food and beverage ante for economy passengers. In addition to a snack bar, a latest mid-flight snack will be offered.

    In a recent development, A retrofit program like this was essential for Aer Lingus to remain competitive in the transatlantic market. The introduction of premium economy was a great move, especially since the cabin is known to be highly profitable.

    According to recent reports, aer Lingus has also done a great job of matching the Irish color scheme and sleek design across all cabins, which is more than can be mentioned for some airlines these days. 😉.

    What do you make of Aer Lingus’ new A330 cabins?

    #30546. Hyatt And Delta Launch Extra Points On Flights And Hotel Stays—But Standard Coach Tickets Don’t Qualify

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 25m • 📚 Deep Dive (4943 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Hyatt And Delta Launch Extra Points On Flights And Hotel Stays—But Standard Coach Tickets Don’t Qualify

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4943 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hyatt and Delta have launched extra points on flights and hotel stays, with airline status, lounge passes and hotel free night awards coming next year.
    • The companies unveiled their partnership in September.
    • Sources indicate that this brings back some of what Hyatt members lost when American Airlines stopped reciprocal points earning at the end of 2024.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hyatt and Delta have launched extra points on flights and hotel stays, with airline status, lounge passes and hotel free night awards coming next year. But there’s a substantial restriction: even a Hyatt Globalist buying a regular Delta coach ticket earns no Hyatt points. That’s not ‘basic economy doesn’t count’ – it’s listerally standard main cabin coach that earns nothing. The companies unveiled their partnership in September. Now we know how the benefits actually work. This brings back some of what Hyatt members lost when American Airlines stopped reciprocal points earning at the end of 2024. But Delta excludes regular coach, gives Hyatt’s lowest elite tier half as many points, and pays hotel guests in a less valuable airline currency (SkyMiles). Who Earns Extra Points And Miles Start by linking your World of Hyatt and Delta SkyMiles accounts. Ongoing extra earning depends on your status: Your Status   Additional Earnings Delta Silver, Gold, Platinum or Diamond Medallion   1 SkyMile per eligible dollar spent with Hyatt, on top of Hyatt points Hyatt Discoverist   1 Hyatt point per $2 of eligible Delta premium cabin spending, on top of SkyMiles Hyatt Explorist, Globalist or Lifetime Globalist   1 Hyatt point per eligible dollar of Delta premium cabin spending, on top of SkyMiles Hyatt status qualifies you for Hyatt points on eligible Delta flights. Delta status qualifies you for SkyMiles on eligible Hyatt spending. For flights, Delta Comfort, Premium Select, First Class and Delta One qualify. Basic, Classic and Extra fare versions qualify when they’re sold in one of those cabins. So basic extra legroom coach qualifies, full fair regular coach doesn’t. . The flight earning rules also require: A Delta marketed and operated flight, with a Delta-issued ticket beginning 006. Your SkyMiles number attached before departure and Hyatt elite status when the flight is completed. A qualifying paid ticket. Eligible spending includes the base fare and airline imposed surcharges, but excludes government taxes, airport fees and amounts paid with miles. These are Hyatt bonus points. They don’t count as base points toward Hyatt status or lifetime Globalist. For hotel spending, eligible room charges, incidentals and qualifying purchases without an overnight stay can earn SkyMiles. Mr & Mrs Smith and The Venetian qualify when booked through Hyatt. Homes & Hideaways and FIND experiences are excluded. Hyatt Nights Can Earn Delta Credits, Lounge Visits And Status Beginning January 1, 2027, linked Hyatt members will have Delta options among their Milestone Rewards. These are choices, so you’ll need to compare them with the other rewards available at the same threshold. The specific awards are: Hyatt Qualification   Delta Reward Choice 20 qualifying nights or 35,000 base points   $25 Delta eCertificate 40 qualifying nights or 65,000 base points   $75 Delta eCertificate 60 qualifying nights or 100,000 base points   $100 Delta eCertificate 70, 80 or 90 qualifying nights   Two single visit Delta Sky Club passes 100 qualifying nights   Delta Gold Medallion status 150 qualifying nights   Delta Platinum Medallion status, without Choice Benefits The flight certificates and lounge passes expire one year after issuance. Each lounge pass covers one person for one visit with a qualifying same-day boarding pass (basic economy passengers excluded). The status awards are for your own account. They don’t provide anything extra if you already hold that tier or higher, and selecting the same status again doesn’t extend it. Platinum at 150 nights is potentially attractive, albeith without the Choice Benefits that normally come with that status (e.g. four Regional Upgrade Certificates). Delta Elites Can Choose Hyatt Free Nights Starting February 1, 2027, for the 2028 Medallion Year, Delta is adding: A Hyatt Category 1–4 free night as a Platinum Choice Benefit. A Hyatt Category 1–7 free night as a Diamond Choice Benefit. These aren’t extra certificates automatically handed to every Platinum and Diamond. You select one instead of another Choice Benefit. No new option to redeem SkyMiles directly for Hyatt free night certificates was announced, like we’d seen with the American partnership. Perhaps the biggest loss is Hyatt redemptions for American Airlines status for a day. Launch Bonuses Don’t Require Elite Status All linked members can participate in the launch offers: November 17–December 31, 2026: Register separately and complete a qualifying Hyatt stay to earn one additional qualifying night credit. That’s one bonus night total, not double nights for the entire stay. January 4–February 15, 2027: Complete your first eligible paid Delta Comfort-or-higher flight to earn 1,000 bonus Hyatt points. January 4–February 15, 2027: Complete your first qualifying Hyatt stay to earn 1,000 bonus SkyMiles. Paid and award stays qualify for the hotel promotions. Mr & Mrs Smith and The Venetian bookings through Hyatt qualify, while Homes & Hideaways doesn’t. The year-end stay must finish after registration and by December 31. For the January hotel offer, checkout must be by February 15. There’s also an Alila Mayakoba trip sweepstakes through November 23. Hyatt notes reciprocal status challenges are coming. Is This Better Than Hyatt’s American Airlines Partnership? There are two different American partnerships to compare against. The original version, which ran through 2024, was better for everyday earning. Hyatt Discoverists earned the same one point per dollar on American airfare as Globalists, and regular coach counted. American elites earned a mile per eligible Hyatt dollar, and those miles also counted as Loyalty Points once that status system was introduced. Delta’s hotel earning has the same nominal mileage rate, but American miles are worth more. And there’s no status credit from those points. American’s final double earning terms also covered eligible FIND and Homes & Hideaways spending, both excluded here. On the flight side you’re earning Hyatt points either way, so the problem isn’t SkyMiles valuation. It’s the cabins that don’t qualify and the halved Discoverist rate. The 2025 American redesign removed double dipping and largely made members pay for partner benefits with their own points or by giving up another reward. Delta restores some actual additional earnings. The milestone comparison is mixed: Flight credits can be more useful than seat coupons. American offered two Preferred Seat coupons at 20 and 30 nights, then two Main Cabin Extra coupons at 40 and 50. Delta status starts later. American Gold was a choice at 70, 80 and 90 Hyatt nights. Delta offers lounge passes there, with its first announced status award at 100 nights. At 150 nights, Delta offers a higher tier. American’s offer topped out at Platinum. Delta Platinum is its third tier, although withholding Choice Benefits takes away a valuable part of the package. American also gave ConciergeKey members Hyatt Globalist and offered Hyatt status choices to other AAdvantage members. We’ll see what reciprocal status offers look like. It’s worth linking accounts and registering for the extra Hyatt night if there’s a stay coming up.     Industry News: Chase Ink Business Preferred Card Bonus: 100K Points Welcome Offer

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1069 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card has a phenomenal sign-up bonus of 100,000 points after spending $8,000 within three first three months, and there’s lots of value to this card in the long term, especially thanks to its reasonable $95 annual fee — read my Ink Preferred review here.
    • This is part of the Chase Ink Business card portfolio, and it’s arguably Chase’s most rewarding and best value business credit card.
    • Link: Learn more about the Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card with 100K bonus points.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card has a phenomenal sign-up bonus of 100,000 points after spending $8,000 within three first three months, and there’s lots of value to this card in the long term, especially thanks to its reasonable $95 annual fee — read my Ink Preferred review here. If you’re eligible for the card, there’s no reason not to apply.

    This is part of the Chase Ink Business card portfolio, and it’s arguably Chase’s most rewarding and best value business credit card. In this post I’d like to go over the Ink Business Preferred bonus details, including eligibility requirements.

    Link: Learn more about the Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card with 100K bonus points.

    The Chase Ink Preferred Card presently has a welcome offer of 100,000 Ultimate Rewards points after spending $8,000 within the first three months.

    Based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Chase Ultimate Rewards points to be worth 1.7 cents each, meaning the 100,000 points are worth $1,700 to me, which is among the best bonuses out there. There are lots of great uses of Chase points, as they can be transferred to all kinds of useful airline and hotel partners.

    Chase Ultimate Rewards partners with programs like Air Canada Aeroplan, Air France-KLM Flying Blue, British Airways Club, United MileagePlus, Virgin Atlantic Flying Club, World of Hyatt, and more. If you want to cash out Chase points (which I wouldn’t recommend), you can get one cent of value per point, meaning the 100,000 points would be worth $1,000.

    Just to give some examples of possible uses of the points, you could transfer 34,000 points to Iberia Club for a one-way Iberia business class ticket from Boston to Madrid, or 60,000 points to Flying Blue for a one-way Air France or KLM business class ticket from Miami to Paris. You can stretch your points even further by taking advantage of transfer bonuses.

    In a recent development, let me emphasize that the Chase Ink Preferred 100K bonus is the best publicly available sign-up bonus that’s at the moment available on the card, and it has been the standard offer since November 2025. How do the previous Chase Ink Preferred offers compare, though?

    As you can see, the Ink Business Preferred sign-up bonus on the card has varied from 80,000 points to 120,000 points, and the current bonus of 100,000 points is 10,000 points better than the previous offer, which was for up to 90,000 points.

    It has been revealed that everyone has to decide for themselves if it’s worth waiting for the possibility of another welcome bonus of over 100,000 points. Personally I probably wouldn’t wait, since we have no reason to believe such an offer is returning soon. Furthermore, with the card’s useful points categories for spending, there’s potentially quite an opportunity cost to waiting. But still, if you’re in no rush, it could be worth waiting.

    When it comes to getting approved for the Chase Ink Preferred Card and earning the welcome bonus, what rules should you be aware of? Well, there are the card specific policies, and then also the more generic Chase policies. When you pull up the application, you’ll see the following terms:.

    The latest cardmember bonus may not be available to you if you have ever had this card. We may also consider factors pertinent to your business in determining your bonus eligibility.

    As you can see, officially the welcome bonus may not be available to you if you right now have this card, or if you’ve had it in the past. However, eligibility for the card (including the bonus) is unrelated to whether you have any other Chase business card.

    It has been revealed that in other words, you’re eligible for this card, including the bonus, if you have other cards from Chase, including cards in the business lineup. Speaking of which, those cards have some amazing bonuses as well, which are worth considering:.

    Beyond that, there are some general Chase rules to be aware of:.

    While Chase business cards can be tough to get approved for, they offer such fantastic bonuses and perks, so it’s worth the effort, in my opinion. Furthermore, it’s nice how the eligibility requirements aren’t too strict in terms of qualifying for the bonus.

    The Chase Ink Preferred Card has a $95 annual fee (with no cost for additional employee cards), and offers all kinds of amazing perks that make it worth holding onto. Among other things, here’s what makes the card so valuable:.

    Let me acknowledge that the Ink Preferred isn’t right for everyone. As I see it, the Ink Preferred is all about the rewards structure and the strong purchase and travel protection, while also having a reasonable cost. If you’re looking for airport lounge access or a card with all kinds of premium perks and credits, then consider the Sapphire Reserve Business, which many people will find to be worthwhile for the Chase Sapphire Lounge access, Priority Pass membership, travel credits, and more.

    The Chase Ink Preferred Card is one of the best business cards out there, and if you’re eligible for the card, there’s lots of merit to applying.

    Not only does the card have a big bonus, but it’s worth holding onto for the great rewards structure, excellent protection benefits, and the ability to maximize other cards in the Chase ecosystem. With the changes we’ve seen to other Chase cards in recent times, this card is arguably even more compelling than in the past.

    Do you have the Chase Ink Preferred Card, and if so, what has your experience been?

    It has been revealed that membership is free and takes no more information than commenting as a guest. Earn status points for good contributions, and see fewer ads as your status grows.

    World Of Hyatt 2027 Updates: Milestone Rewards From 10 Nights, New Rewards, And More

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (953 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, world of Hyatt members can expect more flexibility and choice from January 1, 2027.
    • The update follows the new Hyatt-Delta relationship, which also released this week.
    • Industry observers note that starting January 1, 2027, World of Hyatt members will start enjoying Milestone Rewards after 10 nights stayed or 20,000 base points.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, world of Hyatt members can expect more flexibility and choice from January 1, 2027. Highlights of the update include earning Milestone Rewards sooner, a bunch of new Milestone Rewards, and more flexibility when redeeming rewards and paying for stays. There’s actually no huge catch, and the changes I learned about last night on an intimate call with the Hyatt team are genuinely member-focused.

    The update follows the new Hyatt-Delta relationship, which also released this week.

    Industry observers note that starting January 1, 2027, World of Hyatt members will start enjoying Milestone Rewards after 10 nights stayed or 20,000 base points. That’s great news for relatively infrequent Hyatt guests (like myself), who will no longer have to stay 20 nights or earn 35,000 base points to earn their first Milestone Reward.

    At 10 nights or 20,000 base points, members will be able to choose from:.

    Milestone Rewards will be unlocked at every ten nights, up to 150 nights.

    Not only is it about to become quicker to earn Milestone Rewards, but there’ll also be upcoming awards to choose from each level. Here are a few examples of the 20+ new rewards:.

    The downside of free parking becoming a Milestone Reward means that World of Hyatt members who earn Globalist from 2027 onwards will no longer enjoy it as a permanent status perk on award stays. This will be a notable downgrade to Globalists who value their parking perk.

    Hyatt has published a handy newly introduced infographic with all the details.

    There are also two more important Milestone Reward changes to note, both of which aren’t such positive news:.

    In a recent development, for the first time, World of Hyatt members will be able to stack multiple awards on a single stay. For example, you can use a Suite Upgrade Voucher, a Guest of Honor Award, and claim free parking, all on the same stay.

    According to recent reports, all awards will also expire after 365 of being issued. That’s great for awards that used to only last 180 days.

    According to recent reports, I think this could be my favorite update. Hyatt is enhancing its Pay My Way option to allow guests to choose how to pay for each night of a stay. As someone who struggles to rack up Hyatt points (Hyatt isn’t a transfer partner of any cards in the U.K.), this should certainly streamline booking stays for me.

    The booking page will display each award applied to each individual night and provide guests with a drop-down menu to select how they’d like to pay for each night.

    According to recent reports, at a time when we’re plagued with loyalty program devaluations, these changes coming to World of Hyatt appear to be a genuinely positive slew of updates. Even when you consider some of the less favorable updates, like Globalists losing free parking and some award expiration dates being limited to 365 days, the changes will be positive overall for the vast majority of World of Hyatt members.

    #30543. Breaking: Trump’s ‘invasion’ asylum ban to face justices

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (531 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Trump’s ‘invasion’ asylum ban to face justices

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (531 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Supreme Court agreed on Friday to hear a challenge to President Donald Trump’s claims that an “invasion” at the southern border can be used to deny asylum claims by refugees.
    • The Trump administration had asked the justices to review a decision by the U.S.
    • The administration argues in its petition for the justices to take the case that the president has broad authority over asylum claims, which includes shutting down the system entirely because he has decided he will not grant any.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Supreme Court agreed on Friday to hear a challenge to President Donald Trump’s claims that an “invasion” at the southern border can be used to deny asylum claims by refugees.

    The Trump administration had asked the justices to review a decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit that held the president could not broadly deny asylum claims under federal law. The case is the latest high-profile fight over one of Trump’s signature domestic policies.

    The administration argues in its petition for the justices to take the case that the president has broad authority over asylum claims, which includes shutting down the system entirely because he has decided he will not grant any.

    “The proclamation thus lawfully suspends access to asylum, which is a purely discretionary benefit. The court of appeals’ insistence that aliens are entitled to file futile asylum applications elevates empty procedures over substance,” the petition states.

    Trump issued the order on his first day in office, declaring an “invasion” on the southern border and using that as a reason to deny asylum claims by refugees who present themselves there. The order is still in place, preventing asylum claims at the U.S.-Mexico border while the lawsuit plays out.

    In court filings asking the justices to take the case, the administration pointed to “dramatic” reductions in illegal border crossings, which freed up resources to combat human trafficking and other threats.

    In Friday’s order, the justices agreed to hear arguments over the legality of Trump’s executive order as well as whether the lower-court judge could grant an order in favor of all asylum seekers rather than just the ones who brought the suit.

    Industry observers note that immigration rights groups initially challenged the order and won a successful ruling from a federal judge in Washington. The administration later appealed to the D.C. Circuit, where it lost at a three-judge panel before it brought the case before the justices.

    The D.C. Circuit held that although federal law provides a president discretion in denying asylum claims, he cannot do so categorically.

    The ACLU and immigrant rights groups who brought the case defended the ruling in their own filing. The filing argues that Congress mandated the creation of the asylum system and the president “may not invent by fiat a fresh removal system that eviscerates the protections Congress mandated by statute.”.

    Last term the justices ruled in favor of a separate policy dating to the first Trump administration that allowed officials to prevent asylum claims by stopping refugees from actually reaching the U.S. border.

    A ruling in favor of the refugees could allow the administration to restart that policy and still deny asylum claims.

    Sources indicate that the case granted Friday is the latest high-profile immigration policy clash on the justices’ docket this term. Earlier this year the justices agreed to hear a challenge to the administration’s policy that most immigrants facing deportation should be detained without bond.

    The justices will likely hear oral arguments and decide the case granted Friday before the end of the court’s term next June.

    The case is Mullin v. Refugee and Immigrant Center for Education and Legal Services.
